questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All pastries are chocolates. Some chocolates are cookies. All cookies are cakes. Conclusions: (I) No pastry is a cake. (II) Some cakes are chocolates.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: Some chocolates are cookies and all cookies are cakes, so some chocolates are cakes, that is, some cakes are chocolates (II). Pastries may or may not be cakes, so I does not follow.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 229 ÷ 41 + 502 × 2 – 44 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 229 × 41 − 502 ÷ 2 + 44 = 9389 − 251 + 44 = 9182.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? OPOR, NOPS, ?, LMRU, KLSV
questions.explanation: The first and second letters move back one (O, N, M, L, K and P, O, N, M, L); the third and fourth move forward one (O, P, Q, R, S and R, S, T, U, V). The missing term is MNQT.

questions.text: ‘Simple’ is related to ‘Basic’ in the same way as ‘Difficult’ is related to ‘________’.
questions.explanation: 'Simple' and 'basic' are synonyms; the synonym of 'difficult' is 'complex'.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. Y _ Y _ _ Y _ T _ Y _ Y
questions.explanation: With T, Y, T, Y, Y, T in the blanks the block YTY repeats: YTY YTY YTY YTY.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: All red are green. All green are pink. No pink is blue. Conclusions: I. No green is blue. II. Some blue are red.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: Every green is pink and no pink is blue, so no green is blue (I). Every red is green, so no red is blue either, and II cannot follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FRAMED’ is coded as ‘497621’ and ‘DREAMT’ is coded as ‘769542’. What is the code for ‘T’ in that language?
questions.explanation: FRAMED and DREAMT share D, R, E, A and M, and their codes share 2, 4, 6, 7 and 9. The letter left in DREAMT is T and the digit left in its code is 5, so T = 5.

questions.text: Based on the position in the English alphabetical order, three of the following letter-clusters are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the odd letter-cluster. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: SUZY, PRWV and QSXW move +2, +5, −1 (S → U → Z → Y). MPUT moves +3, +5, −1, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: In a certain code language, FIGURE is coded as ‘VSUGJW’ and COPIED is coded as ‘YMLSWX’. What will be the code for BLANKET?
questions.explanation: Each letter becomes the letter after its opposite (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, ...): F → U → V and C → X → Y. So B → Z, L → P, A → A (Z, wrapping round), N → N, K → Q, E → W and T → H: ZPANQWH.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letters in the word ‘SPIDER’ is arranged in the English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: SPIDER in alphabetical order is D E I P R S. Only I, third in both, keeps its place.

questions.text: Two sets of numbers are given below. In each set of numbers, certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number result(s) in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation(s) on the second number result(s) in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 17 – 19 – 16 – 20; 22 – 24 – 21 – 25

Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (108, 12, 9) (114, 19, 6)
questions.explanation: The first number is the product of the other two: 12 × 9 = 108 and 19 × 6 = 114. Likewise 17 × 8 = 136.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the son of B’; ‘A # B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’; and, ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is M related to T if ‘M # N @ L × P + T’?
questions.explanation: P is T's son, L is P's wife, N is L's father and M is N's sister. So M is T's son's wife's father's sister.

questions.text: Select the triad in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given triads. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (3, 5, 32) (9, 1, 26)
questions.explanation: The third number is the product of the first two plus 17: 3 × 5 + 17 = 32 and 9 × 1 + 17 = 26. Likewise 6 × 1 + 17 = 23.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 30, 22, 36, 75, 178, ?
Select the option that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. OA33, RD36, UG39, XJ42, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move 3 forward (O, R, U, X, then A, wrapping round), as do the second letters (A, D, G, J, M), and the numbers rise by 3: AM45.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 4 – 5 ÷ 9 + 6 × 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 4 + 5 × 9 − 6 ÷ 2 = 4 + 45 − 3 = 46.

questions.text: Three of the following four options are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does NOT belong to that group? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 90 – 99 – 108, 82 – 46 – 10 and 67 – 45 – 23 the numbers change by the same step each time (+9, −36 and −22). 90 – 51 – 13 changes by −39, then −38, so it does not belong.

questions.text: In which of the following games is the ‘Baulk Line’ used?
questions.explanation: In kabaddi the baulk line is marked across each half of the court, and a raider has to cross it during a raid.

questions.text: In the context of cell division, which chromosomal behaviour takes place at the leptotene stage?
questions.explanation: Leptotene, the first stage of prophase I of meiosis, is when the chromosomes begin to condense and become visible. Homologous chromosomes pair (synapsis) in zygotene, and synapsis is complete in pachytene.

questions.text: Nirupama Sanjeev is a famous ______ player of India?
questions.explanation: Nirupama Sanjeev (Nirupama Vaidyanathan) is a former tennis player; at the 1998 Australian Open she became the first Indian woman of the Open era to win a Grand Slam singles match.

questions.text: The ‘Lokranjan’ festival celebrates the folk and tribal culture of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Lokranjan, a festival of folk and tribal dance held every year at Khajuraho, is organised by Madhya Pradesh's Adivasi Lok Kala Academy.

questions.text: How many carbon dioxide and water molecules will be there in the product side, if the following equation is made balanced? C₂H₅OH+O₂→CO₂+H₂O
questions.explanation: Balanced: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O. The two carbon atoms give 2CO₂ and the six hydrogen atoms give 3H₂O.

questions.text: Which playback singer was honoured with the Nightingale of Asia Award in 1987?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Asha Bhosle, the playback singer and younger sister of Lata Mangeshkar, as the 1987 recipient of the Nightingale of Asia Award.

questions.text: To promote agriculture, Muhammad Tughlaq founded which of the following new ministries?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq set up the Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi, a department of agriculture, to bring more land under cultivation.

questions.text: In West Bengal, how many rice crops are grown in a year?
questions.explanation: West Bengal grows three crops of rice a year: aus, aman and boro.

questions.text: Which of the following are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51?
questions.explanation: Part IV of the Constitution, Articles 36 to 51, sets out the Directive Principles of State Policy.

questions.text: Which of the following sectors in India faces seasonal unemployment?
questions.explanation: Farm work is needed mainly at sowing and harvest, so agricultural workers are left without work for part of the year.

questions.text: Arvind Parikh, a Padma Bhushan awardee, plays which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Arvind Parikh is a sitar player of the Etawah (Imdadkhani) gharana and a senior disciple of Ustad Vilayat Khan.

questions.text: ‘Kuki dance’ is a folk dance of India that is predominantly performed in _________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Nagaland. The Kuki dance belongs to the Kuki people, one of Nagaland's recognised tribes (they also live in Manipur and Assam); none of the other states named is their home.

questions.text: The upper portion of the Earth is known as:
questions.explanation: The lithosphere is the Earth's solid outer layer: the crust and the top of the mantle. The troposphere, stratosphere and mesosphere are layers of the atmosphere.

questions.text: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 empowers the _________ to establish authorities charged with the mandate of preventing environmental pollution in all its forms.
questions.explanation: Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 lets the Central Government constitute authorities to prevent, control and abate environmental pollution.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The revolution of 1857 started in May from which of the following cantonments in India?
questions.explanation: The revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857, when the sepoys there mutinied and marched on Delhi.

questions.text: Who among the following famous badminton players won Singapore Open 2022?
questions.explanation: PV Sindhu won the women's singles title at the Singapore Open in July 2022, beating China's Wang Zhi Yi in the final.

questions.text: Which part of Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice President?
questions.explanation: The Vice-President is dealt with in Part V (Articles 63 to 73); Article 66 covers the election.

questions.text: The Gandak river is a tributary of which river?
questions.explanation: The Gandak flows down from Nepal and joins the Ganga in Bihar, opposite Patna.

questions.text: Who among the following Pallava kings occupied Vatapi (Badami) and defeated the Chalukyas?
questions.explanation: Narasimhavarman I took Vatapi in 642, defeating the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II, and took the title 'Vatapikonda'.

questions.text: The term ‘Microfinancing’ was first used in the 1970s during the development of Grameen Bank of Bangladesh, which was founded by ________.
questions.explanation: Muhammad Yunus founded the Grameen Bank, which lends small sums to the poor without collateral; he and the bank shared the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: Light year is the unit of distance.
Light year is the distance travelled by light in one year.
Light year is the unit of time.
questions.explanation: A light year, the distance light travels in a year (about 9.46 × 10¹² km), is a unit of distance, not time. An angstrom (10⁻¹⁰ m) is a unit of length.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles and Parts of the Indian Constitution deal with the State Legislature?
questions.explanation: Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI deal with the State Legislature. Articles 214 to 231 cover the High Courts, 79 to 122 Parliament and 243 to 243-O the Panchayats.

questions.text: What is the economic justification for subsidies in the agriculture sector?
options: It is used to provide benefits for capital goods producers in agriculture.
It is mostly used to provide benefits for rich farmers.
It is a part of government expenditure in the service sector.
It is an incentive to provide the benefits of advanced technology and decrease the cost of production.
questions.explanation: Farm subsidies, on fertiliser for instance, were justified as an incentive for farmers, small farmers above all, to adopt new technology such as high-yielding varieties, and as a way to lower the cost of production.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of both mammals and birds?
questions.explanation: Mammals and birds are both warm-blooded. Pneumatic (air-filled) bones are found only in birds, and birds lay eggs, whereas most mammals give birth to live young.

questions.text: In a class of 150 students (boys and girls only), the girls are 60. The average weight of boys is 52 kg and that of girls is 48 kg. What is the average weight (in kg) of the whole class?

Three people, A, B and C, invest in a business in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. It was decided that 9% of the profits will go to charity. If the total profit was ₹2,50,000, then find the share of C in the profit (in ₹).
questions.explanation: After 9% goes to charity, 91% of ₹2,50,000 = ₹2,27,500 is shared. C gets 5/10 of it: ₹1,13,750.

questions.text: Given a linear equation in two variables: 5x + 7y - 8 = 0, which of the following linear equations, along with the given equation, forms a system of linear equations having no solution?
questions.explanation: Two lines have no common solution when they are parallel: the coefficients in the same ratio but not the constants. 5/5 = 7/7 ≠ −8/−16, so 5x + 7y − 16 = 0. (10x + 14y − 16 = 0 is the same line, with infinitely many solutions.)

questions.text: If ₹1,875 becomes ₹2,625 in 4 years, what will ₹24,000 become at the end of 9 years at the same rate of interest, under simple interest?
questions.explanation: The interest on ₹1,875 for 4 years is ₹750, so the rate is 750/(1,875 × 4) × 100 = 10%. On ₹24,000 for 9 years: 24,000 × 10 × 9/100 = ₹21,600, so the amount is ₹45,600.

questions.text: If (48°+ k) is an acute angle and sin(48°+ k) = cos 13°, what is the value of k(in °)?
questions.explanation: sin(48° + k) = cos 13° = sin 77°, and both angles are acute, so 48° + k = 77° and k = 29°.

questions.text: Find the remainder when 9²⁰ + 2 is divided by 4.
questions.explanation: 9 leaves remainder 1 on division by 4, so 9²⁰ does too; 1 + 2 = 3.

questions.text: A number whose fifth part increased by 5 is equal to its third part decreased by 7. Find half of the number.
questions.explanation: x/5 + 5 = x/3 − 7, so x/3 − x/5 = 2x/15 = 12 and x = 90. Half of it is 45.

questions.text: Two athletes are participating in a race on a circular track of 220 m. Ravi runs at the speed of 22 m/s, while Kapil runs at the speed of 11 m/s. They start from the same point, at the same time and in the same direction. After how many seconds will they meet for the first time?
questions.explanation: Running the same way, Ravi gains 22 − 11 = 11 m/s on Kapil. They meet when he has gained a full lap: 220/11 = 20 seconds.

questions.text: A person first increases the price of a commodity by 8% and then he announces a discount of 18%. The actual discount (in%) on the original price is:
questions.explanation: 1.08 × 0.82 = 0.8856 of the original price, an actual discount of 11.44%.

questions.text: If books bought at prices ranging from ₹200 to ₹260 are sold at prices ranging from ₹250 to 300, what is the greatest possible profit that might be made in selling 25 books?
questions.explanation: The greatest profit comes from buying at ₹200 and selling at ₹300: ₹100 a book, so ₹2,500 on 25 books.

questions.text: From a point A, which is at a distance of 17 cm from the centre C of a circle with radius 8 cm, the pair of tangents AB and AD to the circle are drawn. The area of the quadrilateral ABCD is _____ cm².
questions.explanation: Tangent length = √(17² − 8²) = √225 = 15 cm, and each radius meets its tangent at a right angle. ABCD is two right triangles of area ½ × 8 × 15 = 60 cm²: 120 cm² in all.

questions.text: If the angles of a triangle are in the ratio 7 : 8 : 3, then the value of the largest angle is:
questions.explanation: The angles are 7, 8 and 3 parts of 180°, 10° a part, so the largest is 8 × 10° = 80°.

questions.text: One pipe can fill a tank four times as fast as another pipe. If together the two pipes can fill the tank in 48 minutes, the slower pipe alone will be able to fill the tank in:
questions.explanation: If the slower pipe takes t minutes, the faster takes t/4: 1/t + 4/t = 5/t = 1/48, so t = 240 minutes.

questions.text: In a room, there are some chairs and some people. If on each chair, only one person is seated, then there is no chair for exactly one person. If on each chair, two persons sit, then there is one vacant chair. What is the number of chairs in the room?
questions.explanation: With c chairs there are c + 1 people; seated two to a chair they fill c − 1 chairs. 2(c − 1) = c + 1, so c = 3.

questions.text: Two successive percentage decrease of 25% each is by what percentage less than two successive percentage increase of 25% each? (Round to two decimal places.)
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Ranveer never has the habit of “making a beeline” for his academic activities.
questions.explanation: To 'make a beeline for' something is to go straight to it, quickly.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Rohit did not slap Kunal.
options: Kunal was not slapped by Rohit.
Kunal had not been slapped by Rohit.
Kunal was not being slapped by Rohit.
Kunal has not been slapped by Rohit.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'did not slap' becomes 'was not slapped' in the passive: 'Kunal was not slapped by Rohit.'

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The teacher asked him not to keep disturbing the class, but it had no affect.
questions.explanation: 'Affect' is a verb; the noun needed after 'no' is 'effect': 'but it had no effect'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. I do not have any “access” to the information in this matter.
questions.explanation: 'Access' is the right or means to reach something; its opposite is 'denial'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who looks at the bright side of things/situations
questions.explanation: An optimist looks on the bright side; a pessimist expects the worst.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The company understood that these small protests of employees regarding low wages were just “the tip of the iceberg”.
options: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is really much greater
A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is solvable
A large part of a problem which is really noticeable
A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is non-existent
questions.explanation: 'The tip of the iceberg' is the small visible part of a much larger problem.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to replace the word in brackets. The author's writing was so captivating that readers were [enthralled], while the other book left them completely uninterested.
questions.explanation: 'Enthralled' means captivated, held spellbound; its opposite is 'bored'. 'Interested' and 'intrigued' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank. Akshaya ______________ hard for the entrance exam and received a high score.
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the past ('received a high score'), so the simple past 'studied'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Even when he was left with plenty of fortune, he lived a “frugal” life.
questions.explanation: 'Frugal' means careful with money: 'thrifty'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. He was the most “honest” and good-hearted man that she had ever met.
questions.explanation: 'Honest' means truthful and straightforward: 'sincere'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence. A. The world’s biggest radio telescope is in Puerto Rico. B. It is called Arecibo dish. C. It was built 40 years ago. D. It is also 300 metres across.
questions.explanation: Only A can open: it introduces the telescope that B, C and D each call 'It'. B names it, D adds its size ('also') and C its age: ABDC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. This library building is very “high” and has 25 floors.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'high' is 'low'.

questions.text: In the given question, a statement divided into different segments is given. Rearrange all the segments to form a coherent statement. O: that the Soviet army had liberated P: from the fascist forces came under Q: the east European countries R: the control of the USSR S: after the Second World War
questions.explanation: 'After the Second World War (S) the east European countries (Q) that the Soviet army had liberated (O) from the fascist forces came under (P) the control of the USSR (R).'

questions.text: Select the sentence that contains a spelling error.
options: The venerated singer was also secretive, moody and very intense, famous for erratic and difficult behaviour
Elephants are in trouble mainly because people desire ivory trinkets that are made of tusks, often gruesomely killing them to achieve their purpose.
Researchers recommend that pesticides should not be used indiscriminately as they eliminate biodiversity for future generations.
Journalism is often the work of painstaking rigour and perseverence that detail the socio-political experiences of our worlds.
questions.explanation: 'Perseverence' should be 'perseverance'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Will you give me an independent project?
options: Would an independent project be given?
Would I be given an independent project?
Will I be given an independent project by you?
Will you be given an independent project by me?
questions.explanation: The indirect object 'me' becomes the subject of the passive question: 'Will I be given an independent project by you?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. RN Right’s literary works helped redefine discussions “in race relations in America” in the mid-20th century.
questions.explanation: Discussions are 'of' (or about) a subject: 'discussions of race relations in America'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Profuse
questions.explanation: 'Profuse' means plentiful; its opposite is 'scarce'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. His parents didn’t allow him to enrol in the arts college because he is a “dabbler in arts, science or literature.”
questions.explanation: A dilettante dabbles in the arts or a subject without serious study. A connoisseur is an expert judge in matters of taste, and an ignoramus knows nothing.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'receive': 'i' before 'e' except after 'c'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The chair I have bought recently “is costly” than what I bought last year.
questions.explanation: A comparison with 'than' needs the comparative: 'is costlier than'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. 2022 sees us entering a third year of the pandemic, and the harm 1________ children is increasingly evident: A record rise in child poverty. Setbacks to progress on 2_________ vaccinations. Disruption to education for entire generation. That harm 3________ as an unintended side effect of the world's efforts to manage the crisis.  COVID has been a uniquely dis-equalizing crisis. Lopsided 4________ vaccines aside, learning losses have been greatest among poorest children, and job losses have been disproportionately borne by women and youth.  What next for the world’s children in the year ahead? As in the past two years, prospects for children will continue to hinge 5________ on the pandemic and how it is managed.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: 'The harm done to children': harm is 'done to' someone.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. 2022 sees us entering a third year of the pandemic, and the harm 1________ children is increasingly evident: A record rise in child poverty. Setbacks to progress on 2_________ vaccinations. Disruption to education for entire generation. That harm 3________ as an unintended side effect of the world's efforts to manage the crisis.  COVID has been a uniquely dis-equalizing crisis. Lopsided 4________ vaccines aside, learning losses have been greatest among poorest children, and job losses have been disproportionately borne by women and youth.  What next for the world’s children in the year ahead? As in the past two years, prospects for children will continue to hinge 5________ on the pandemic and how it is managed.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: 'Routine vaccinations', the regular childhood immunisations, whose progress the pandemic set back.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. 2022 sees us entering a third year of the pandemic, and the harm 1________ children is increasingly evident: A record rise in child poverty. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: 'That harm' is singular, so 'has emerged', the present perfect for an effect still being felt.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: 'Lopsided access to vaccines': unequal availability of them.
