questions.text: Select the term from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the given series. HM71, JP68, LS65, NV62, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +2 (H, J, L, N, P), second letters +3 (M, P, S, V, Y) and the numbers fall by 3 (71, 68, 65, 62, 59): PY59.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (24, 15, 120) (21, 19, 133) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each set, first × second ÷ 3 = third: 24 × 15 ÷ 3 = 120 and 21 × 19 ÷ 3 = 133. Likewise 27 × 12 ÷ 3 = 108.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. CRW: TIN :: DOZ: UFQ :: ALW:?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 9 places back, wrapping round after A: C → T, R → I, W → N and D → U, O → F, Z → Q. So A → R, L → C and W → N: RCN.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different. Note : The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: SQPN, YWVT and NLKI move −2, −1, −2. WVTS moves −1, −2, −1, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘EAGLE’ is written as ‘DZFKD’ and ‘DREAM’ is written as ‘CQDZL’. How will ‘SINCE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place back: EAGLE → DZFKD and DREAM → CQDZL. So SINCE → RHMBD.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially place from left to right in the blanks below to balance the given equation. 75 _ 3 _ 17 _ 8 = 0

All the six members of a family, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, live together. 2 is the daughter of 3, but 3 is not the mother of 2. 1 and 3 are a married couple. 5 is the sister of 3. 4 is the daughter of 1. 6 is the brother of 2. Who is the mother of 2?
questions.explanation: 3 is a parent of 2 but not the mother, so 3 is 2's father. 1 is married to 3, so 1 is 2's mother.

questions.text: The question contains pairs of words that are related to each other in a certain way. Three of the following four word pairs are alike as these have the same relationship and thus form a group. Which word pair is the one that DOES NOT belong to that group? (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters / number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.explanation: A book is made up of pages, a flower of petals and spectacles of lenses: whole and part. Shoes are worn on the feet; feet are not a part of shoes.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 35, 46, 68, 101, 145, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 11, 22, 33, 44, so the next is 55: 145 + 55 = 200.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. Z _ A _ Z _ _ Z A _ Z _
questions.explanation: With Z, Z, A, Z, Z, A in the blanks the block ZZA repeats: ZZA ZZA ZZA ZZA.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will change if each of the letters in the word ‘CORNFLAKES’ is re-arranged in the English alphabetical order from left to right?
questions.explanation: In alphabetical order CORNFLAKES becomes ACEFKLNORS. Only L (sixth) and S (tenth) keep their places, so eight letters change position.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some vegetables are fruits. Some fruits are flowers. All flowers are garlands. Conclusions: I. Some garlands are fruits. II. Some vegetables are flowers. III. Some vegetables are garlands.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Some fruits are flowers and all flowers are garlands, so some fruits are garlands, and some garlands are fruits (I). Nothing links vegetables to flowers or garlands for certain, so II and III do not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'EXCESS' is written as '726572121', 'ENERGY' is written as '716720927', how will 'ESCAPE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet plus 2: E → 7, X → 26, C → 5, S → 21. So ESCAPE → 7, 21, 5, 3, 18, 7: 72153187.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? CQJG, ERMJ, ?, ITSP, KUVS
questions.explanation: First letters move +2 (C, E, G, I, K), second letters +1 (Q, R, S, T, U), third letters +3 (J, M, P, S, V) and fourth letters +3 (G, J, M, P, S): GSPM.

questions.text: Which number will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 27 × 3 + 4 ÷ 2 − 7 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 27 ÷ 3 − 4 × 2 + 7 = 9 − 8 + 7 = 8.

questions.text: 11 is related to 121 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 22 is related to 484. To which of the following is 31 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to its square: 11² = 121 and 22² = 484. So 31² = 961.

questions.text: The same operation(s) are followed in all the given number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 22 : 45, 7 : 15 and 5 : 11 the second number is twice the first plus 1. 11 : 121 is a square (11²), so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 4 : 68 :: 8 : 136 :: 9 : ? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 17 times the first: 4 × 17 = 68 and 8 × 17 = 136. Likewise 9 × 17 = 153.

questions.text: The record obtained by the measurement of earthquake is called a:
questions.explanation: A seismogram is the record made by a seismograph, the instrument that measures earthquake waves; seismology is the study of earthquakes.

questions.text: Ghiyas ud-din Balban had set up a _________ department called 'Diwan-i-arz'.
questions.explanation: The Diwan-i-Arz was the military department, in charge of recruiting, equipping and paying the army; Balban used it to strengthen his forces.

questions.text: In chess which of the following may move only diagonally?
questions.explanation: The bishop moves only diagonally. The queen moves both straight and diagonally, the rook only straight, and the knight in an L shape.

questions.text: Which of the following is associated with the retreating monsoon in India?
questions.explanation: As the monsoon retreats in October and November, high temperature and humidity make the weather oppressive: the 'October heat'. The loo blows in summer, mahawat is winter rain from western disturbances, and kaal baisakhi is a pre-monsoon storm.

questions.text: Which famous santoor player was honoured with the Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan Award in 1998?
questions.explanation: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma, the santoor maestro, received the Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan Award in 1998.

questions.text: The Atal Innovation Mission was launched in year ________.
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog set up the Atal Innovation Mission in 2016 to promote innovation and entrepreneurship.

questions.text: In 2022, Vinay Mohan Kwatra took charge as the Foreign Secretary of India. Prior to this, he served as the ambassador to which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: Vinay Mohan Kwatra was India's ambassador to Nepal before he became Foreign Secretary in May 2022.

questions.text: Alla Rakha is famous for playing which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Ustad Alla Rakha was a celebrated tabla player, and the father of Zakir Hussain.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who suggested the law that the British Government passed in 1856 to support widow remarriage?
questions.explanation: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar's campaign and petitions led to the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act of 1856.

questions.text: Ishwari Prasad is credited to have introduced the ________ Gharana of Kathak.
questions.explanation: Ishwari Prasad is regarded as the founder of the Lucknow gharana of Kathak.

questions.text: Pulakeshin II assumed the title of ‘Dakshinapatheshvara’ (lord of the south) after defeating which of the following rulers of north India?
questions.explanation: Pulakeshin II, the Chalukya king of Badami, defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada and stopped his advance into the Deccan.

questions.text: Makar Sankranti is the festival dedicated to which of the following Lords?
questions.explanation: Makar Sankranti marks the sun's entry into Makara (Capricorn) and is dedicated to Surya, the sun god.

questions.text: When did a States Reorganisation Commission was set up, which recommended the creation of linguistic States on the basis of larger linguistic groups?
questions.explanation: The States Reorganisation Commission under Fazl Ali was set up in December 1953; its report led to the States Reorganisation Act of 1956.

questions.text: According to Census of India 2011, female adolescents in the age group of 10-19 years had a share of:
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 47.3%: the share of girls among India's adolescents (aged 10-19) in the 2011 census, against 52.7% boys.

questions.text: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the Election Commission?
questions.explanation: Part XV (Articles 324 to 329) deals with elections; Article 324 vests their superintendence in the Election Commission.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an eastern coast port?
questions.explanation: Chennai is on the east coast, on the Bay of Bengal; Mumbai, Mormugao and New Mangalore are west-coast ports.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In 1910, The United India House at Seattle, USA, was set up by ___________.
options: Tarak Nath Das and GD Kumar
questions.explanation: Tarak Nath Das and G.D. Kumar set up the United India House at Seattle in 1910.

questions.text: An organic reaction used to convert an aryl diazonium salt into an aryl halide using a copper(I) halide catalyst is called:
questions.explanation: In the Sandmeyer reaction a copper(I) halide replaces the diazonium group of an aryl diazonium salt with a halogen. The Gattermann reaction uses copper powder and a halogen acid instead.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for protecting and improving the environment and safeguarding forests and wildlife?
questions.explanation: Article 48A, a Directive Principle added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, asks the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.

options: GDP + Net factor income from abroad
GDP – Net factor income from abroad
questions.explanation: Net domestic product is gross domestic product less depreciation (the consumption of fixed capital). Adding net factor income from abroad to GDP gives GNP.

questions.text: What is the primary objective of the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act of 2006 in India?
options: To increase import tariffs to protect MSMEs
To focus on large-scale industries only
To promote and facilitate the development of MSMEs
questions.explanation: The MSMED Act, 2006 provides for facilitating the promotion and development of micro, small and medium enterprises and enhancing their competitiveness.

questions.text: Where was the Durand Cup Tournament started in India in 1888?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Shimla, where the Durand Cup, Asia's oldest football tournament, was started in 1888; it is named after Sir Mortimer Durand, then India's Foreign Secretary.

questions.text: Which essential amino acid enhances calcium absorption and also plays an important role in the formation of collagen?
questions.explanation: Lysine, an essential amino acid, helps the body absorb calcium and is needed for the formation of collagen.

questions.text: According to Mendeleev's Periodic Table, which elements’ properties matched up remarkably well with eka-silicon?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev left a gap for eka-silicon and predicted its properties; germanium, discovered in 1886, matched them closely.

questions.text: The salaries of P and Q together amount to ₹9,60,000. P and Q save 64% and 44%, respectively of their individual salaries. If P’s expenditure is 1.5 times Q’s expenditure, then what is the ratio of P’s salary to Q’s salary?
questions.explanation: P spends 36% of his salary and Q 56%. 0.36P = 1.5 × 0.56Q = 0.84Q, so P : Q = 0.84 : 0.36 = 7 : 3.

questions.text: The side BC of ∆ABC is produced to a point D. If AC = BC and ∠BAC = 70°, then find the value of ∠ACD − ∠ABC.
questions.explanation: AC = BC, so the angles opposite them are equal: ∠ABC = ∠BAC = 70° and ∠ACB = 40°. ∠ACD = 180° − 40° = 140°, so ∠ACD − ∠ABC = 70°.

questions.text: Rohini buys a Bluetooth headphone set for ₹1,700 from a wholesale shop and marks it at ₹2,000. Later on, she allows a discount of 40% on its sale. What is her loss or gain percentage (correct up to two decimal places)?
It is always possible to draw a circle passing through ______ non-collinear points in a plane.
questions.explanation: Any three non-collinear points lie on exactly one circle: the circumcircle of the triangle they form.

questions.text: The simple interest on a sum for 6 years is three-fifth of the sum. The rate of interest per annum is:
The average of the squares of the first 48 natural numbers is
questions.explanation: The sum of the squares of 1 to n is n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6, so their average is (n + 1)(2n + 1)/6 = 49 × 97/6 = 792.17.

questions.text: Nihira is 25 years old and Punith is 30 years old. How many years ago was the ratio of their ages 3 : 4?
Suppose P starts walking at a speed of 8 km/h. After 8 hours B started travelling on a bicycle at a speed of 24 km/h. The distance from the starting B can catch A is:
questions.explanation: In 8 hours the walker covers 8 × 8 = 64 km. B gains 24 − 8 = 16 km/h, so he catches up in 64/16 = 4 hours, having ridden 24 × 4 = 96 km.

questions.text: If the lengths of two sides of an isosceles triangle are 6 cm and 12 cm, then find the length of the third side.
questions.explanation: The third side equals one of the other two. If it were 6 cm, then 6 + 6 = 12 would not exceed the third side and no triangle could form; so it is 12 cm (sides 6, 12 and 12).

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P) achieve success Q) when you R) and polite S) stay humble
questions.explanation: 'Stay humble (S) and polite (R) when you (Q) achieve success (P).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Leela was in class when the big fight happened. So, if you want to know the details, You should ask her, you will get the truth “given by somebody who is directly involved and therefore likely to be accurate.”
questions.explanation: To hear something 'straight from the horse's mouth' is to hear it from the person directly involved.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My dog / barks / very louder / at night.
questions.explanation: 'Barks' needs an adverb, not a comparative adjective: 'barks very loudly'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Dissolve
questions.explanation: To 'dissolve' can mean to fade away or disappear; its opposite is 'appear'. 'Fade' and 'vanish' are close in meaning to it.

questions.text: The following sentence contains a word with a spelling error. Rectify the sentence by selecting the correct spelling of the identified word from the given options. Later on, he was truely apologetic for his misconduct in the meeting.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'truly': the 'e' of 'true' is dropped.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'exhilaration'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Laudable
questions.explanation: 'Laudable' means deserving praise; its opposite is 'deplorable'. 'Commendable' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. A comic play was performed by the comedian.
options: The comedian do perform a comic play.
The comedian performance a comic play.
The comedian performed a comic play.
The comedian performs a comic play.
questions.explanation: The past passive 'was performed by' becomes the simple past active: 'The comedian performed a comic play.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The research team is conducting experiments on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease.
options: Experiments are conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease from the research team.
Experiments were being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team.
Experiments have been conducted on a new drug that could have revolutionised the treatment of the disease through the research team.
Experiments are being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'is conducting' becomes 'are being conducted', with the agent at the end: 'by the research team'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word to fill in the blank. Ram “failed” initially but after a few years, he _________ in every field.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'failed' is 'succeeded'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The company specialises at / designing, crafting and manufacturing / exquisite, high-quality furniture / of exceptional craftsmanship.
questions.explanation: 'Specialise' takes the preposition 'in', not 'at': 'The company specialises in designing'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Derogatory
questions.explanation: 'Derogatory' means showing a low opinion of someone: 'insulting'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Raj is very interested in studying human psychology, so he decided to pursue his master’s degree in __________.
questions.explanation: The study of the human mind and behaviour is 'psychology'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined part in the following sentence. The entire speech of the revivalist “fell flat with” the crowd that was present there.
options: had somewhat of a result on
questions.explanation: A speech that 'falls flat with' an audience fails to have any effect on it.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A performer’s first public appearance
questions.explanation: A 'debut' is a performer's first public appearance.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. To go through an area making a lot of noise and causing damage
questions.explanation: To 'rampage' is to rush about noisily and violently, causing damage.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (A) and was searching for them (B) the grandmother couldn’t find (C) all around the house (D) placed them on her head (E) her spectacles because she had
questions.explanation: 'The grandmother couldn't find (B) her spectacles because she had (E) placed them on her head (D) and was searching for them (A) all around the house (C).'

questions.text: Select the option that can substitute/replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence. If he runs, he (get) there in time.
questions.explanation: A first conditional: 'if' with the present ('runs') in one clause and 'will' with the verb in the other: 'he will get there in time'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. We went to a “legitimate” Mexican restaurant for my birthday, where they served cuisine like you would find in Mexico.
questions.explanation: 'Legitimate' here means real or authentic: 'genuine'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Our university is “affiliated” with various institutes all over the world.
questions.explanation: 'Affiliated' means officially connected: 'allied'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Kuno Palpur National Park, located in Madhya Pradesh's Chambal (1)__________, has an area of 750 square kilometres. It now has leopards, jackals, spotted deer, sambhar, neelgai, chinkara, wild boar, and four-horned antelope, making it a perfect (2)_________ base for felids. Despite strong objections from Gujarat, which (3)_________ that lions were part of the state's heritage, that MP had a poor (4)________ in wildlife management, and that Kuno Palpur had other big cat species that would (5)___________ lion relocation, the sanctuary was chosen for the lion reintroduction project in 2013.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The park lies in the Chambal 'region' of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Kuno Palpur National Park, located in Madhya Pradesh's Chambal (1)__________, has an area of 750 square kilometres. It now has leopards, jackals, spotted deer, sambhar, neelgai, chinkara, wild boar, and four-horned antelope, making it a perfect (2)_________ base for felids. Despite strong objections from Gujarat, which (3)_________ that lions were part of the state's heritage, that MP had a poor (4)________ in wildlife management, and that Kuno Palpur had other big cat species that would (5)___________ lion relocation, the sanctuary was chosen for the lion reintroduction project in 2013.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The animals listed are what big cats hunt: a 'prey base' for felids.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Kuno Palpur National Park, located in Madhya Pradesh's Chambal (1)__________, has an area of 750 square kilometres. It now has leopards, jackals, spotted deer, sambhar, neelgai, chinkara, wild boar, and four-horned antelope, making it a perfect (2)_________ base for felids. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Gujarat 'claimed' that lions were part of its heritage, one of its objections to the move.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Kuno Palpur National Park, located in Madhya Pradesh's Chambal (1)__________, has an area of 750 square kilometres. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A poor 'record' in wildlife management: a poor past performance.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Kuno Palpur National Park, located in Madhya Pradesh's Chambal (1)__________, has an area of 750 square kilometres. Despite strong objections from Gujarat, which (3)_________ that lions were part of the state's heritage, that MP had a poor (4)________ in wildlife management, and that Kuno Palpur had other big cat species that would (5)___________ lion relocation, the sanctuary was chosen for the lion reintroduction project in 2013.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Other big cats that would 'jeopardise' (endanger) the lions' relocation; 'safeguard' says the opposite.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 66, 75, 86, 99, 114, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 9, 11, 13, 15, rising by 2 each time, so the next is 17: 114 + 17 = 131.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 139 + 40 ÷ 5 − 168 × 3 = 283
Select the correct combination of letters that when sequentially filled in the blanks of the given series will make the series logically complete. B_FH_LNP_T_X
questions.explanation: The series takes every second letter: B D F H J L N P R T V X. The blanks are D, J, R and V.

questions.text: ‘Obstinate’ is related to ‘Stubborn’ in the same way as ‘Resolute’ is related to ‘________’. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.explanation: 'Obstinate' and 'stubborn' mean the same, as do 'resolute' and 'determined'.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if all the letters in the word RICKET are arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: In alphabetical order RICKET becomes C E I K R T. Only K (fourth) and T (sixth) keep their places.

questions.text: Two sets of numbers are given below. In each set of numbers, certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number result(s) in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation(s) on the second number result(s) in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 8 – 33 – 66 – 81; 11 – 36 – 72– 87

18 is related to 90 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 31 is related to 155. To which of the following is 52 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 5: 18 × 5 = 90 and 31 × 5 = 155. So 52 × 5 = 260.

questions.text: 17 is related to 102 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 29 is related to 174. To which of the following is 39 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 6: 17 × 6 = 102 and 29 × 6 = 174. So 39 × 6 = 234.

questions.text: All the alphabets in the word ‘CARDBOARD’ are arranged in the alphabetical order. How many alphabets are there in the English alphabetical series between the alphabet which is fourth from the left end and the one which is second from the right end in the newly formed cluster of nine letters?
questions.explanation: CARDBOARD in alphabetical order is A A B C D D O R R. The fourth from the left is C and the second from the right is R; between C and R come D to Q: 14 letters.

questions.text: Three of the following four options are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does NOT belong to that group? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The middle number is twice the difference of the outer two: 2 × (80 − 36) = 88, 2 × (62 − 34) = 56 and 2 × (51 − 23) = 56. In 68 – 54 – 94, 2 × (94 − 68) = 52, not 54.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow from the statements. Statements: All papers are pencils. All pencils are erasers. All erasers are pens. Conclusions: I. All pens are papers. II. Some papers are erasers. III. Some pens are pencils.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All papers are pencils and all pencils are erasers, so some papers are erasers (II). All pencils are erasers and so pens, so some pens are pencils (III). I does not follow: papers lie inside pens, not pens inside papers.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘CLERK’ is written as ‘BKEQJ’ and ‘OFFICE’ is written as ‘OEEIBE’. How will ‘POST’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each consonant moves one letter back and each vowel stays: CLERK → BKEQJ and OFFICE → OEEIBE. So POST → OORS.

questions.text: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd man out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
questions.explanation: In QST, IKL and ACD the letters move +2, then +1. TWW moves +3, then 0, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the son of B’, A − B means ‘A is the wife of B’, A × B means ‘A is the brother of B’ and A ÷ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. Based on the above, how is T related to P if ‘P − M + R ÷ T × S’?
questions.explanation: P is the wife of M, M is the son of R, R is the mother of T and T is the brother of S. M and T are both R's sons, so T is P's husband's brother.

questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 15 + 5 × 8 – 72 ÷ 4 + 16 × 3 = 101

Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. EYES : FTFZ :: MIND : OENJ :: REST : ?
questions.explanation: The two halves swap places and each letter moves one forward: EY ES → ES EY → FTFZ and MI ND → ND MI → OENJ. So RE ST → ST RE → TUSF.

questions.text: In the following series, only one letter-cluster is incorrect. Select the incorrect letter-cluster. ZXU SQN LKI ECZ XVS
questions.explanation: In ZXU, SQN, ECZ and XVS the letters step back 2, then 3 (in ECZ, C − 3 wraps round to Z), and each cluster starts 7 letters before the last. LKI steps back 1, then 2; the cluster should be LJG.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘DRAPE’ is coded as ‘65432’ and ‘TAPED’ is coded as ‘24596’. What is the code for ‘R’ in that language?
questions.explanation: D, A, P and E are in both words, as are 6, 5, 4 and 2 in both codes. The letter left in DRAPE is R and the digit left in its code is 3, so R = 3.

questions.text: Which of the following states is one of those states that have no Panchayati Raj Institution at all?
questions.explanation: Under Article 243M, Part IX (the panchayats) does not apply to Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram, which keep their own traditional village councils.

questions.text: In which month is the Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) located around 20°N-25°N latitude (over the Gangetic plain)?
questions.explanation: By NCERT's account, in July the ITCZ lies around 20°N-25°N over the Gangetic plain, where it is called the monsoon trough.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of capital receipts?
options: Revenue from the sale of government assets
questions.explanation: Selling government assets (disinvestment) brings in a capital receipt, as it reduces the government's assets. Taxes, interest and grants are revenue receipts.

questions.text: Jaipal Singh Munda is associated with which of the following sports?
questions.explanation: Jaipal Singh Munda captained India's hockey team at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, where India won its first Olympic hockey gold.

questions.text: In January 2023, Koneru Humpy won India’s first-ever silver medal at the __________ held in Almaty, Kazakhstan.
questions.explanation: Koneru Humpy won silver in the women's section of the World Blitz Chess Championship at Almaty, which ended on 30 December 2022: the first medal by an Indian woman at that event.

questions.text: Bihu festival is the main festival of which state?
questions.explanation: Bihu, celebrated three times a year (Bohag, Kati and Magh Bihu), is the main festival of Assam.

questions.text: The New Moore Island is in geographic proximity to:
questions.explanation: New Moore Island (South Talpatti) rose in the Bay of Bengal off the mouth of the Hariabhanga river, on the India-Bangladesh border, and was claimed by both countries.

questions.text: During the period of 1947 to 1990, how many five-year plans were completed?
questions.explanation: Seven plans ran in this period, from the First (1951-56) to the Seventh (1985-90); the Eighth began only in 1992.

questions.text: Who among the following sent Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.explanation: Seleucus I Nicator sent Megasthenes as his envoy to Chandragupta Maurya's court at Pataliputra, which Megasthenes described in his 'Indica'.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Aves (birds) class?
questions.explanation: Pteropus is the flying fox, a fruit bat, and so a mammal. Psittacula (parakeets), Struthio (the ostrich) and Neophron (the Egyptian vulture) are birds.

questions.text: When you take Lead nitrate powder in a boiling tube and heat it, you will observe the emission of brown fumes that are of _____________________.
questions.explanation: Heated lead nitrate breaks down into lead oxide, nitrogen dioxide (the brown fumes) and oxygen: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂.

questions.text: Which of the following playback singers is the recipient of the Karnataka Ratna Award 2005?
questions.explanation: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, the Hindustani vocalist from Karnataka, received the Karnataka Ratna in 2005.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: ‘Drain of Wealth’, a critique of the colonial exploitation, was given by which of the following nationalist leaders?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji set out the drain theory in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who founded the Theosophical Society in New York in 1875?
options: Baba Dayal Das and Madan Lal
Madame HP Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott
Naoroji Furdunji and Satyendra Nath Bose
questions.explanation: Madame H. P. Blavatsky and Colonel H. S. Olcott founded the Theosophical Society in New York in 1875; it later made Adyar, Madras, its headquarters.

questions.text: Mirabai Chanu secured a silver medal at which Commonwealth Games?
questions.explanation: Mirabai Chanu won silver in the women's 48 kg weightlifting at the 2014 Glasgow Commonwealth Games; she won gold in 2018 and 2022.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who is the author of the book ‘From Plassey to Partition and After : A History of Modern India’?
questions.explanation: 'From Plassey to Partition and After' is Sekhar Bandyopadhyay's history of modern India.

questions.text: Who has written the book Sangeet Bal Prakash?
questions.explanation: Vishnu Digambar Paluskar wrote 'Sangeet Bal Prakash', a three-volume series of music textbooks for students.

questions.text: What is the name of the inflammatory condition that causes cracks, crusting and scaling at the corners of the mouth due to vitamin B2 deficiency?
questions.explanation: Cheilosis (angular cheilitis), cracking and scaling at the corners of the mouth, is a classic sign of riboflavin (vitamin B2) deficiency.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers originates from the Himalayas?
questions.explanation: The Ganga rises from the Gangotri glacier in the Himalayas. The Narmada, Tapi and Godavari are peninsular rivers.

questions.text: Which of the following Delhi sultans introduced two coins, namely silver tanka and copper jital?
questions.explanation: Iltutmish introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital, the two basic coins of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.text: In Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awaas Yojana, the cost of unit assistance is shared between Central and State Governments in the ratio ___________ for the North-Eastern and the Himalayan states.
questions.explanation: Under PMAY-G the Centre and the states share the unit cost 60 : 40 in the plains and 90 : 10 in the North-Eastern and Himalayan states.

questions.text: As per article 158, the Governor shall NOT be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State specified in ________ Schedule.
questions.explanation: Article 158(1) bars the Governor from being a member of Parliament or of the legislature of any state specified in the First Schedule.

questions.text: Name the straight chain alkane having chemical formula C₉H₂₀, which is used as a research chemical and in making biodegradable detergents.
questions.explanation: Alkanes are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, so the one with nine carbon atoms, C₉H₂₀, is nonane. Dodecane has 12 carbons, nonadecane 19 and icosane 20.

questions.text: According to the Tea Board of India’s report (2021-22), which group of states in India is the largest tea producer?
questions.explanation: Assam and West Bengal produce most of India's tea, Assam being the largest producer.

questions.text: If a 12-year-old is found to be working in a factory manufacturing carpets, which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India will be violated?
questions.explanation: Article 24 prohibits employing children below the age of 14 in factories, mines or other hazardous work.

questions.text: In the 8th class, consisting of 30 students, a Mathematics test was taken. 10 students had an average score of 90. The other students had an average score of 75. What is the average score of the whole class?
The relation between K₁ and K₂ for which the system of linear equations K₁x + 3y = 8 and 4x + K₂y = 16 represents coincident lines, is:
questions.explanation: Coincident lines need K₁/4 = 3/K₂ = 8/16 = 1/2, so K₁ = 2 and K₂ = 6: K₂ = 3K₁.

questions.text: In a quadrilateral ABCD, AB = BC, AD = DC. ∠ABD = 68°, ∠ADB = (2y-7)°, ∠BDC = 33°, ∠DBC = (3x+2)°. Then the value of 2x+3y is:
questions.explanation: Triangles ABD and CBD are congruent (SSS), so ∠DBC = ∠ABD and ∠ADB = ∠BDC. Then 3x + 2 = 68, x = 22, and 2y − 7 = 33, y = 20: 2x + 3y = 44 + 60 = 104.

questions.text: Find the value of tan 72° − tan 27° − tan 72° tan 27°.
questions.explanation: tan 45° = (tan 72° − tan 27°)/(1 + tan 72° tan 27°) = 1, so tan 72° − tan 27° = 1 + tan 72° tan 27° and the expression is 1.

questions.text: A policeman noticed a thief at some distance. The policeman started running to catch the thief and the thief also started running at the same time. The speed of both policeman and the thief was 12 km per hour and 10 km per hour, respectively. It took 30 minutes for the policeman to catch the thief. Find the initial distance (in metres) between them.
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 12 − 10 = 2 km/h, so in 30 minutes he closes 1 km: they started 1,000 m apart.

questions.text: A man loses 28% by selling an article for ₹144. If he sells it for ₹288, what will be his gain/loss percentage?
questions.explanation: CP = 144/0.72 = ₹200. Selling for ₹288 gains ₹88, which is 44% of ₹200.

questions.text: If A:B = 6 : 8 and B:C = 5 : 11, then A:B:C is:

Naman borrows a sum of ₹3,48,020 at the rate of 8% per annum simple interest. At the end of the first year, he repays ₹15,090 towards return of principal amount borrowed. If Naman clears all pending dues at the end of the second year, including interest payment that accrued during the first year, how much does he pay (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
questions.explanation: First-year interest = 8% of ₹3,48,020 = ₹27,841.60. After the ₹15,090 repayment the principal is ₹3,32,930, earning ₹26,634.40 in the second year. Final payment = 3,32,930 + 27,841.60 + 26,634.40 = ₹3,87,406.

questions.text: The two circles intersect at two points P and Q. PR and PS are diameters of the two circles. What is ∠PQR ?
questions.explanation: PR is a diameter, so ∠PQR is an angle in a semicircle: 90°.

questions.text: Find the diameter (in cm) of a circle whose circumference is equal to the sum of the circumferences of two circles of radii 12 cm and 16 cm.
questions.explanation: 2πR = 2π × 12 + 2π × 16, so R = 28 cm and the diameter is 56 cm.

questions.text: If m is even, then (8ᵐ – 1) is divisible by:
questions.explanation: With m = 2n, 8ᵐ − 1 = 64ⁿ − 1, which is divisible by 64 − 1 = 63.

questions.text: The ratio of expenditure to savings of a woman is 4 : 1. If her income and expenditure are increased by 20% and 10%, respectively, then find the percentage change in her savings.
questions.explanation: Take income 5, expenditure 4 and savings 1. The new income is 6 and the new expenditure 4.4, so savings become 1.6: a 60% rise.
Brackets first: 25 − 8 + 24 = 41, and 5 + 3 × (25 − 20) = 5 + 15 = 20 ('of' means multiply). Then 41 + 78 − 20 = 99.

questions.text: Find the value of 'k' for which the system of equations 4x+6y=7 and 6x+(k+4)y-21=0 has a unique solution.
questions.explanation: A unique solution needs 4/6 ≠ 6/(k + 4), that is k + 4 ≠ 9: k ≠ 5.

questions.text: Select the sentence that does NOT have a spelling error.
options: She is very particular about pronounciation in her classes.
The movie was very successful in the urban areas, but not among rural audiences.
There wedding was during the summer, which is why we didn’t attend it.
There were no intermittent showers in the city, as was predicted during the whether forecast.
questions.explanation: 'Pronounciation' should be 'pronunciation', 'there wedding' 'their wedding' and 'whether forecast' 'weather forecast'.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P- for a Q- exercise daily R- one must S- good body
questions.explanation: 'One must (R) exercise daily (Q) for a (P) good body (S).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The ship launched out on a “journey by water or sea” of discovery.
questions.explanation: A voyage is a long journey by sea or water: 'a voyage of discovery'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Nominal
questions.explanation: 'Nominal' means very small, or existing in name only; its opposite is 'significant'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Ashoka was the greatest “than all the Mauryan Emperors” .
questions.explanation: A superlative takes 'of', not 'than': 'the greatest of the Mauryan Emperors'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who eats human flesh.
questions.explanation: A cannibal is a person who eats human flesh.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He and his friends / does not / want to / attend the meeting.
questions.explanation: A subject joined by 'and' is plural: 'He and his friends do not want to attend the meeting.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Bombastic
questions.explanation: 'Bombastic' means high-sounding and pompous; its opposite is 'simple'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice. He had cleaned the bathroom.
options: The bathroom had been cleaned by him.
The bathroom has been cleaned by him.
The bathroom has cleaned by him.
The bathroom had cleaned by him.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had cleaned' becomes 'had been cleaned': 'The bathroom had been cleaned by him.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment in which the article has been used INCORRECTLY. In the recent past, the IT industry has emerged / as a major contributor to an industry revenue / as well as employment / opportunity provider in the country.
options: as a major contributor to an industry revenue
In the recent past, the IT industry has emerged
questions.explanation: 'Revenue' here is uncountable and takes no 'an': 'a major contributor to industry revenue' (or 'to the industry's revenue').

questions.text: Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Why didn’t she bring her son to my house?
options: Why isn’t her son brought to my house?
Why wasn’t her son brought to my house?
Why wasn’t her son brought by her to my house?
Why isn’t her son brought by you to my house?
questions.explanation: The past simple 'didn't bring' becomes 'wasn't brought', with the agent kept: 'Why wasn't her son brought by her to my house?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Forgive
questions.explanation: To forgive is to stop feeling resentment towards someone; SSC's key gives 'loathe', to hate intensely, as its opposite. 'Requite' (to pay back a wrong) is also arguable; 'clear' and 'unburden' are close to forgiving.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined part of the following sentence. My brother always received “the lion’s share” of every meal that we had.
questions.explanation: The 'lion's share' is the largest part of something.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence. Parul is known as a rigteous and honest lady.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'righteous'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined part in the following sentence. We all have to “pull our socks up” for the upcoming Board exam, if we want to get outstanding grades.
questions.explanation: To 'pull one's socks up' is to make an effort to do better: to work harder than before.

questions.text: Select the option that can substitute/replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence. I said I (don’t) understand.
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb the reported present moves back: 'I said I didn't understand.'

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (a) the Industrial Revolution denotes (b) and continued until the middle of the 19th century (c) a significant period of social, economic and technological revolution (d) that commenced in the latter part of the 18th century
questions.explanation: 'The Industrial Revolution denotes (a) a significant period of social, economic and technological revolution (c) that commenced in the latter part of the 18th century (d) and continued until the middle of the 19th century (b).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. He said that he lacks the ___________ to stand in a queue. (patience)
questions.explanation: 'Endurance', the ability to bear something unpleasant without giving up, is close to 'patience' here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in the brackets to fill in the blank. The pool was too ______ at this end for kids to play. [SHALLOW]
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'shallow' is 'deep': the pool was too deep at this end for children.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Concede
questions.explanation: To 'concede' is to admit that something is true; its opposite is to 'deny'. 'Surrender' is close in meaning.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We naturally seek the company of those whose (1) _________ are the same as our own. Fools do not like the (2) _________ of wise men, and wise men avoid fools. Serious-minded people do not find much in common with (3) _________ folk, and vice versa. Sinners feel uncomfortable with (4) _________ and do not seek their company. We can, therefore, as a rule, judge a man’s (5) _________ by the company he keeps.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: We seek the company of those whose 'tastes' are the same as our own.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We naturally seek the company of those whose (1) _________ are the same as our own. Fools do not like the (2) _________ of wise men, and wise men avoid fools. Serious-minded people do not find much in common with (3) _________ folk, and vice versa. Sinners feel uncomfortable with (4) _________ and do not seek their company. We can, therefore, as a rule, judge a man’s (5) _________ by the company he keeps.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Fools do not like the 'company' of wise men: the passage is about the company we keep.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We naturally seek the company of those whose (1) _________ are the same as our own. Fools do not like the (2) _________ of wise men, and wise men avoid fools. Serious-minded people do not find much in common with (3) _________ folk, and vice versa. Sinners feel uncomfortable with (4) _________ and do not seek their company. We can, therefore, as a rule, judge a man’s (5) _________ by the company he keeps.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Frivolous' (not serious) folk are the opposite of the serious-minded.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We naturally seek the company of those whose (1) _________ are the same as our own. Fools do not like the (2) _________ of wise men, and wise men avoid fools. Serious-minded people do not find much in common with (3) _________ folk, and vice versa. Sinners feel uncomfortable with (4) _________ and do not seek their company. We can, therefore, as a rule, judge a man’s (5) _________ by the company he keeps.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Sinners are uncomfortable with 'saints', their opposites.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We naturally seek the company of those whose (1) _________ are the same as our own. Fools do not like the (2) _________ of wise men, and wise men avoid fools. Serious-minded people do not find much in common with (3) _________ folk, and vice versa. Sinners feel uncomfortable with (4) _________ and do not seek their company. We can, therefore, as a rule, judge a man’s (5) _________ by the company he keeps.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: We judge a man's 'character' by the company he keeps.

questions.text: ‘LISP’ is related to ‘ORHK’ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ‘WAND’ is related to ‘DZMW’. To which of the following is ‘BOTE’ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y and so on): L → O, I → R, S → H, P → K and W → D, A → Z, N → M, D → W. So BOTE → YLGV.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letters in the word ‘DOWNSIZE’ is re-arranged in the English alphabetical order from left to right?
questions.explanation: DOWNSIZE in alphabetical order is D E I N O S W Z. D (1st) and N (4th) keep their places: two letters.

questions.text: 19 is related to 76 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 27 is related to 108. To which of the following is 49 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 4: 19 × 4 = 76 and 27 × 4 = 108. Likewise 49 × 4 = 196.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: In UOW, LFN and PJR the letters move −6, then +8. IAK moves −8, then +10, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: 14 is related to 42 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 26 is related to 78. To which of the following is 47 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 3: 14 × 3 = 42 and 26 × 3 = 78. Likewise 47 × 3 = 141.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘÷’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘+’ are interchanged? 2 × 16 ÷ 36 + 42 − 6 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 2 + 16 − 36 × 42 ÷ 6 = 2 + 16 − 252 = −234.

questions.text: Select the number that will come in the place of the question mark(?), if ‘+’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged 61 – 42 × 6 ÷ 9 + 27 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 61 + 42 ÷ 6 × 9 − 27 = 61 + 63 − 27 = 97.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'CASE' is written as 'FTBD' and 'CAKE' is written as 'FLBD'. How will 'CALF’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and each letter moved one place forward: CASE → ESAC → FTBD and CAKE → EKAC → FLBD. So CALF → FLAC → GMBD.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 45 : 56 :: 62 : 73 :: 19 : ? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 11 more than the first: 45 + 11 = 56 and 62 + 11 = 73. Likewise 19 + 11 = 30.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question marks (?) in the given series? 88, 78, 70, 64, 60, ?, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −10, −8, −6, −4, shrinking by 2 each time, so the next two are −2 and 0: 60 − 2 = 58, then 58 − 0 = 58.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? AEYT, CGWR, EIUP, ? , IMQL
questions.explanation: First and second letters move forward 2 (A, C, E, G, I and E, G, I, K, M); third and fourth letters move back 2 (Y, W, U, S, Q and T, R, P, N, L): GKSN.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the given letter series. C A R E T _ R C A _ E T C R C A R _ T C R _ A R E T _ R C A
questions.explanation: With C, R, E, C, C in the blanks the block CARETCR repeats: CARETCR CARETCR CARETCR CARETCR CA.

questions.text: ‘Tame’ is related to ‘Wild’ in the same way as ‘Adjacent’ is related to ‘________’. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.explanation: 'Tame' and 'wild' are opposites, as are 'adjacent' (next to) and 'distant'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the husband of B’, A − B means ‘B is the mother of A’, A × B means ‘B is the sister of A’ and A ÷ B means ‘A is the daughter of B’. Based on the above, how is Q related to T if ‘P + Q × R − S ÷ T’?
questions.explanation: P + Q: P is Q's husband, so Q is female. Q × R: R is Q's sister. R − S: S is R's mother, and so Q's. S ÷ T: S is T's daughter. So Q is T's daughter's daughter.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BREAK’ is coded as ‘57123’ and ‘BROKE’ is coded as ‘91753’. What is the code for ‘A’ in that language?
questions.explanation: B, R, E and K are in both words, as are 5, 7, 1 and 3 in both codes. The letter left in BREAK is A and the digit left in its code is 2, so A = 2.

questions.text: The same operation(s) are followed in all the given number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 11 : 143, 13 : 169 and 15 : 195 the second number is 13 times the first. 12 × 13 = 156, not 152, so 12 : 152 is the odd pair.

questions.text: Hola Mohalla is a festival associated with which religion/belief?
questions.explanation: Hola Mohalla is a Sikh festival held at Anandpur Sahib the day after Holi, begun by Guru Gobind Singh with displays of martial skill.

questions.text: What action was taken by the government to celebrate the achievement of the Green Revolution in agriculture?
options: Distributed free food to all the people
Distributed green vegetables to the people
Released a regular salary for the farmers
questions.explanation: In July 1968 a commemorative postage stamp, 'Wheat Revolution', was released to mark the Green Revolution's record wheat harvests.

questions.text: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts led to formation of the Goods and Services Tax Council?
questions.explanation: The 101st Amendment Act, 2016, which introduced GST, inserted Article 279A providing for the GST Council.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following Acts gave the government enormous powers to repress political activities, and allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for two years?
questions.explanation: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 let the government repress political activity and detain political prisoners without trial for two years.

questions.text: The term Blue Line is associated with which of the following games?
questions.explanation: In ice hockey two blue lines divide the rink into the attacking, neutral and defending zones.

questions.text: India finished on which of the following positions in overall medals tally at Commonwealth games 2022?
questions.explanation: At the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham India won 61 medals (22 gold) and finished fourth, behind Australia, England and Canada.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In November 2021, the government declared November 15 as ‘Janjatiya Gaurav Divas’. It happens to be the birth anniversary of which of the following freedom fighters?
questions.explanation: Janjatiya Gaurav Divas marks the birth anniversary of the tribal leader Birsa Munda, born on 15 November 1875.

questions.text: Which acid is used as a souring agent added to vinegar, pickled vegetables, and sauces, and as a raw material for seasoning?
questions.explanation: Vinegar is a dilute solution of acetic (ethanoic) acid, which gives it its sour taste.

questions.text: Which of the following gases plays an important role in welding titanium, aluminium, stainless steel, and magnesium?
questions.explanation: Argon, an inert gas, is used as a shielding gas in welding: it keeps oxygen and nitrogen in the air away from the hot metal.

questions.text: In the southern ranges of which hills is Mawsynram, which receives the highest rainfall in the world, located?
questions.explanation: Mawsynram lies in the southern part of the Khasi hills in Meghalaya.

questions.text: In which year was Ujala Yojana launched?
questions.explanation: UJALA (Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All), which distributes LED bulbs at low cost, was launched in January 2015.

questions.text: Which coal is low-grade, brown and soft with high moisture content?
questions.explanation: Lignite is a low-grade brown coal, soft and with a high moisture content; Neyveli in Tamil Nadu has India's main reserves.

questions.text: Which award was started by the Government of Madhya Pradesh in 1980 to the exponents of Hindustani classical music?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh instituted the Tansen Samman, named after the musician of Akbar's court, in 1980 for exponents of Hindustani classical music.

questions.text: For which of the following tribal music and dance forms was Arjun Singh Dhurve conferred with Tulsi Samman?
questions.explanation: Arjun Singh Dhurve of Dindori, Madhya Pradesh, is an exponent of the Baiga tribal dance; he received the Tulsi Samman and, in 2022, the Padma Shri.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding circular flow of income?
options: In a circular flow, leakages are equal to injections.
The income of one sector becomes the expenditure of the other.
The real flow and monetary flow move in a circular manner in an opposite direction.
Savings as well as government expenditure are injections to the circular flow.
questions.explanation: Savings are a leakage from the circular flow of income, not an injection; government expenditure, investment and exports are injections.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that the ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as best to subserve the common good’?
questions.explanation: Article 39(b), a Directive Principle, asks the State to distribute ownership and control of the community's material resources to subserve the common good.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Khudai Khidmatgars, a non-violent movement among the Pathans was started by ______.
questions.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, the 'Frontier Gandhi', founded the Khudai Khidmatgars (the 'Red Shirts') in 1929.

questions.text: How many athletes were selected to represent India at the 1924 Paris Summer Olympics?
questions.explanation: Eight athletes were picked at the All India Olympic Games, held in Delhi in February 1924, to represent India at the Paris Olympics.

questions.text: The type of reaction that is typically found when a material that is required for the reaction to proceed, such as a surface or a catalyst, is saturated by the reactants is called a __________ order reaction.
questions.explanation: When the catalyst or surface is saturated, the rate no longer depends on the reactants' concentration: a zero order reaction.

questions.text: Where was the first successful textile mill established in India?
questions.explanation: The first successful textile mill in India was set up in Mumbai (then Bombay) in 1854.

questions.text: The registered office of the Sangeet Natak Akademi is at:
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy of music, dance and drama, has its office at Rabindra Bhavan, New Delhi.

questions.text: To gain control over Kannauj the Tripartite Struggle was fought between which of the following dynasties?
questions.explanation: The Gurjara-Pratiharas, the Rashtrakutas and the Palas fought over Kannauj for about two centuries from the 8th century.

questions.text: Which of the following schemes of the Government of India is a part of the ‘Target Group’ approach?
options: Command Area Development & Water Management Programme (CADP)
questions.explanation: The Small Farmers and Marginal Farmers Development Agencies were aimed at groups of people (the target-group approach); the hill area, drought-prone area and command area programmes were aimed at regions (target areas).

questions.text: A tap can fill a cistern in 10 minutes and another tap can empty it in 12 minutes. If both the taps are open, the time (in hours) taken to fill the tank will be:
questions.explanation: With both taps open the cistern fills at 1/10 − 1/12 = 1/60 of its volume a minute, so it takes 60 minutes: 1 hour.

questions.text: The ratio of circumference and diameter of a circle is 3 : 5. If the circumference is 6 cm, then the radius of the circle is:
questions.explanation: Diameter = 6 × 5/3 = 10 cm, so the radius is 5 cm. (In a real circle the ratio is π : 1; the question's 3 : 5 is used as given.)

questions.text: The monthly income of Ramesh in year 2021 was ₹18,600 and his monthly expenditure was ₹12,400. In year 2022 his income increased by 15% and his expenditure increased by 8%. Find the percentage increase in his savings.

Pranav borrows a sum of ₹335180 at the rate of 13% per annum simple interest. At the end of the first year, he repays ₹23060 towards return of principal amount borrowed. If Pranav clears all pending dues at the end of the second year, including interest payment that accrued during the first year, how much does he pay (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
A well with 14 cm radius is dug 23 cm deep. Find the volume of the earth taken out of it.

Seema walks around a circular field at the rate of 3 rounds per hour, while Priya runs around it at the rate of 8 rounds per hour. They start in the same direction from the same point at 11:54 p.m. They shall first cross each other at:
questions.explanation: Priya gains 8 − 3 = 5 rounds an hour on Seema, so she first catches up after 1/5 hour = 12 minutes: 11:54 p.m. + 12 minutes = 12:06 a.m.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 6?
questions.explanation: A number divisible by 6 must be even with a digit sum divisible by 3. 438750 is even and its digits add up to 27; 128530's add up to 19, and 62233 and 12581 are odd.

questions.text: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 60, and that of the rest is 80. What is the average score of the class?

From a point T, a tangent TP at point P, is drawn to a circle with centre O. A secant TQR (point Q is near to point T) is drawn from the point T. ∆PQR is inscribed into the circle by joining the points P, Q and R. Draw lines OQ and OR. If ∠PTQ is 27° and ∠ TPQ = 55°, what is the degree measure of ∠ROQ?
questions.explanation: In ΔTPQ, ∠PQT = 180° − 27° − 55° = 98°, so ∠PQR = 82°. By the alternate segment theorem ∠PRQ = ∠TPQ = 55°, so ∠QPR = 180° − 82° − 55° = 43°. The central angle ∠ROQ is twice that: 86°.

questions.text: Cindy bought 15 apples and 12 oranges and paid a sum of ₹447 for the purchase. Which of the statements given below is inconsistent with the information given in the previous statement, leading to no possible prices of the two fruits?
options: Purchased 10 apples and 13 oranges and paid a sum of ₹353
Purchased 25 apples and 20 oranges and paid a sum of ₹745
Purchased 35 apples and 28 oranges and paid a sum of ₹1,029
Purchased 12 apples and 8 oranges and paid a sum of ₹340
questions.explanation: 15 apples and 12 oranges cost ₹447, so 5 apples and 4 oranges cost ₹149. 35 apples and 28 oranges are 7 times that and must cost ₹1,043, not ₹1,029. The other three fit an apple at ₹21 and an orange at ₹11.

questions.text: The single discount equivalent to the discount series of 15%, 20% and 5% is:
questions.explanation: 0.85 × 0.80 × 0.95 = 0.646 of the price is paid, so the single discount is 35.4%.

questions.text: In ∆PQR, S and T are the midpoints of the sides PQ and PR, respectively. The length of the side QR is 12 cm. If ST is parallel to QR, then find the length (in cm) of ST.
questions.explanation: By the midpoint theorem the segment joining the midpoints of two sides is half the third side: ST = 12/2 = 6 cm.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. His father’s arm was bandaged by the kind nurse.
options: The kind nurse bandaged his father’s arm.
The kind nurse bandages his father’s arm.
The kind nurse has bandaged his father’s arm.
The kind nurse had bandaged his father’s arm.
questions.explanation: 'Was bandaged' is the simple past passive, so the active is in the simple past: 'The kind nurse bandaged his father's arm.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The “betrayer of the country” was at last unmasked.
questions.explanation: A traitor is one who betrays his or her country; a truant stays away from school without leave.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Please go and meet the chairperson. / She will be / away for the / few next days.
options: Please go and meet the chairperson.
questions.explanation: The usual order is 'the next few days', not 'the few next days'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence. I picked up my little clock and it began to “dance gracefully”.
questions.explanation: A clock does not dance; it chimes: 'it began to chime prettily'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. We should clean the house regularly.
options: The house should be cleaned regularly by us.
The house should be being cleaned regularly by us.
The house should be clean regularly by us.
The house should have been cleaned regularly by us.
questions.explanation: A modal passive is modal + 'be' + past participle: 'should clean' becomes 'should be cleaned'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. It was his “decency” that he employed him.
questions.explanation: 'Decency' here means good, considerate behaviour: 'courtesy'.

questions.text: Read the sentence carefully and select the ANTONYM of the underlined word from the given options. I heard his suggestion but I am quite “unsure” about the risks involved in it.
questions.explanation: 'Unsure' means doubtful; its opposite is 'certain'. 'Doubtful' is a synonym.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Summative assessment is the assignment of the student’s performance at the end of the academic term. B. This new pattern ensures that besides just textbook teaching and learning, effective child-teacher interaction is encouraged. C. The CBSE envisages two types of examinations, Formative and Summative. D. Formative assessment is a part of the teaching-learning process and is done through conversation, quizzes, interviews, projects, assignments, etc.
questions.explanation: C introduces the two types of examination, D and A describe formative and summative assessment in that order, and B sums up the new pattern: C, D, A, B.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The line, 'Round the rugged rocks the ragged rascal ran' uses “the repetition of usually initial consonant sounds in two or more neighbouring words or syllables” .
questions.explanation: Alliteration is the repetition of the same initial consonant sound in neighbouring words, as in 'rugged rocks' and 'ragged rascal ran'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. While I was walking to the store, my friend calls me and ask for a favour.
options: my friend calls me and ask
questions.explanation: The sentence is set in the past ('was walking'), so 'my friend called me and asked'; 'calls … ask' also mixes two tenses.

questions.text: Select the option that substitutes the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. In any time of crisis, there is always one mument that stands out from all the others.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'moment'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in the brackets to fill in the blank. She left the party ______ because of her parents’ strict time restrictions. [late]
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'late' is 'early': her parents' strict rules made her leave early.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. The soldier struck the enemy with the “short sword fixed onto the end of the gun.”
questions.explanation: A bayonet is a blade fixed to the muzzle of a rifle; a baton is a short stick.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The mother couldn’t _________ such an insult from her son in front of the others.
questions.explanation: To 'bear' an insult is to put up with it; 'bier', 'beer' and 'bare' sound alike but mean something else.

questions.text: Select the sentence that contains a spelling error.
options: Fermented apple juice is touted to have many health benefits though most are anecdotal and not supported by scientific facts.
It is important for scientists to acknowledge their humanity and the implications of their inventions.
Intriguing as it is, the house was never sold because it was thought to be haunted.
There are many believes about ancient artefacts that some of them are patently not true.
questions.explanation: 'Believes' is a verb; the plural noun is 'beliefs': 'many beliefs about ancient artefacts'.

questions.text: Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. Due to her impoverished state, most of her relatives “treated her with contempt.”
options: Gave a wide space to her
Turned up their nose at her
questions.explanation: To 'turn up one's nose at' someone is to treat them with contempt.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence. (P) hard work and perseverance (Q) no matter how difficult (O) lead to success (R) the journey may seem
questions.explanation: 'Hard work and perseverance (P) lead to success (O) no matter how difficult (Q) the journey may seem (R).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. Ruby gave her mother a hug and offered to knead the ________.
questions.explanation: Dough is made by kneading 'flour', which sounds the same as 'flower'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Let the dust settle
options: To wait for a situation to become clear or certain
Wait for the other person to make a move
To make use of a situation
questions.explanation: To 'let the dust settle' is to wait until a confused situation calms down and becomes clear.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The rise in global temperature (1)__________ already occurred is leading to extreme weather events that bring (2)__________ heat waves and droughts, devastating floods and increasingly powerful hurricanes and tropical storms. The combination of these factors means the impact on human health is increasing and is (3)__________ accelerate. But there is room for hope, particularly if governments take action now to (4)__________ the pledges made at Glasgow in November 2021 and to go further in resolving the climate crisis. WHO is (5)__________ governments to lead a just, equitable, and fast phase out of fossil fuels and transition to a clean energy future.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'The rise … that has already occurred': 'rise' is singular, and the present perfect goes with 'already'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
