questions.explanation: 'Regardless of' means without regard to; 'notwithstanding' and 'nevertheless' do not take 'of'.

questions.text: ‘Noise’ is related to ‘Silence’ in the same way as ‘Light’ is related to ‘________’.
questions.explanation: Silence is the absence of noise, as darkness is the absence of light: each pair are opposites.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All computers are printers. Some printers are laptops. All laptops are mobiles. Conclusions: I.Some printers are computers. II.Some laptops are printers. III. Some mobiles are laptops.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow.
Only conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All computers are printers, so some printers are computers (I). Some printers are laptops, so some laptops are printers (II). All laptops are mobiles, so some mobiles are laptops (III). All three follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TIDE’ is coded as ‘9457’ and ‘DENT’ is coded as ‘7593’. What is the code for ‘N’ in that language?
questions.explanation: T, D and E are in both words, as are 9, 5 and 7 in both codes. The letter left in DENT is N and the digit left in its code is 3, so N = 3.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? EQBY, GPDX, ?, KNHV, MMJU
questions.explanation: First letters move forward 2 (E, G, I, K, M), second letters back 1 (Q, P, O, N, M), third letters forward 2 (B, D, F, H, J) and fourth letters back 1 (Y, X, W, V, U): IOFW.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion/s logically follow/s from the given statements. Statements: Some telephones are curtains. All curtains are lamps. No lamps is books. Conclusions: (I) All lamps are telephones. (II) No books is lamps.
questions.explanation: No lamp is a book, so no book is a lamp (II). Only some telephones are known to be curtains, and so lamps, so not every lamp need be a telephone: I does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘What you think you become’ is written as ‘Fe Mo Su Ta Za’ and ‘What you think you achieve’ is written as ‘Mo Su Te Fe Za’. How will ‘achieve’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'What you think you' is in both sentences, as are the codes Fe, Mo, Su and Za. The word left in the second sentence is 'achieve' and the code left is Te, so achieve = Te.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the given letter series. M N _ O J K M _ Q O J K _ N Q _ J K M N Q O _ K M N
questions.explanation: With Q, N, M, O, J in the blanks the block MNQOJK repeats: MNQOJK MNQOJK MNQOJK MNQOJK MN.

questions.text: 34 is related to 191 by certain logic. Following the same logic, 56 is related to 301. To which of the following is 63 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is five times the first plus 21: 34 × 5 + 21 = 191 and 56 × 5 + 21 = 301. Likewise 63 × 5 + 21 = 336.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is 5 related to 2 if ‘5 ÷ 1 × 3 ÷ 4 − 2’?
questions.explanation: 5 is the father of 1, 1 is the wife of 3, 3 is the father of 4, and 4 is the brother of 2. So 1 is 2's mother, and 5 is 2's mother's father.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: In LPN, HLJ and BFD the letters move +4, then −2. GIK moves +2, then +2, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: 27 is related to 119 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 33 is related to 143. To which of the following is 42 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is four times the first plus 11: 27 × 4 + 11 = 119 and 33 × 4 + 11 = 143. Likewise 42 × 4 + 11 = 179.

questions.text: Select the number that will come in the place of the question mark(?), if ‘+’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged 31 ÷ 3 – 186 × 6 + 17 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 31 × 3 + 186 ÷ 6 − 17 = 93 + 31 − 17 = 107.

questions.text: The same operation(s) are followed in all the given number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 45 : 54, 35 : 42 and 55 : 66 the second number is 6/5 of the first (9 × 5 and 9 × 6, and so on). 40 × 6/5 = 48, not 52, so 40 : 52 is the odd pair.

questions.text: ‘ACKO’ is related to ‘ZXPL’ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ‘HIND’ is related to ‘SRMW’. To which of the following is ‘PUKE’ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet: A ↔ Z, C ↔ X, K ↔ P, O ↔ L, and H ↔ S, I ↔ R, N ↔ M, D ↔ W. So P → K, U → F, K → P and E → V: KFPV.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 8 : 79 6 : 51
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first plus 15: 8² + 15 = 79 and 6² + 15 = 51. Likewise 9² + 15 = 96.

questions.text: Each of the letters in the word ‘LASTING’ is arranged in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical series between the letter which is second from the left end and the one which is fourth from the right end in the new letter-cluster thus formed?
questions.explanation: LASTING in alphabetical order is A G I L N S T. The second from the left is G and the fourth from the right is L; between them come H, I, J and K: four letters.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 949, 1006, 1066, 1129, 1195, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 57, 60, 63 and 66, rising by 3, so the next is 69: 1195 + 69 = 1264.

questions.text: What will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 63 × 9 + 21 – 4 ÷ 5 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 63 ÷ 9 − 21 + 4 × 5 = 7 − 21 + 20 = 6.

questions.text: Which of the following articles from Directive Principles of state policy mentions about organization of Village Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Article 40, a Directive Principle, asks the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government.

questions.text: Who among the following sports persons is designated as brand ambassador for Nikshay Mitra, an initiative under Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan by Ministry of Health and Family welfare of GOI in November 2022?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Paralympian Deepa Malik. Nikshay Mitras are individuals and organisations who support TB patients through their treatment under the Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan.

questions.text: Which of the following was the mascot of the Khelo India University Games 2022?
questions.explanation: The mascot of the Khelo India University Games 2022, held in Uttar Pradesh, was Jitu, a barasingha (swamp deer), the state animal.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the aims of National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) of India is/are correct? 1.To make agriculture more productive. 2.To make agriculture more sustainable. 3.To promote organic farming.
questions.explanation: The NMSA aims to make agriculture more productive, sustainable, remunerative and climate resilient, and its Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana component promotes organic farming.

questions.text: On 29th October 2020, the Ministry of Science and Technology launched the SERB-POWER Scheme. What is the objective of the scheme?
options: To strengthen the solar programme of India with France
To mitigate gender disparity in science and engineering research funding in various academic programmes and laboratories
To allow reservation for women in the Parliament and Judiciary
To allow reservation for women in the Ministry of Science and Technology
questions.explanation: SERB-POWER (Promoting Opportunities for Women in Exploratory Research) supports women scientists, to narrow the gender gap in research funding.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Samata Sainik Dal was formed in 1927 by whom among the following personalities?
questions.explanation: B. R. Ambedkar founded the Samata Sainik Dal in 1927.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a halogen gas?
questions.explanation: Helium is a noble gas (Group 18). Fluorine, chlorine and bromine are halogens (Group 17).

questions.text: Deimachus who was a Greek ambassador came to India during the reign of the Mauryan king, _________.
questions.explanation: Deimachus was sent by the Seleucid king Antiochus I to the court of Bindusara, Chandragupta Maurya's son.

questions.text: Which of the following countries has the highest Hindu population after India?
questions.explanation: Nepal, where about four in five people are Hindus, has the largest Hindu population after India.

questions.text: Indira PP Bora is a Padma Shri Awardee 2020 for her contribution to which Indian classical dance?
questions.explanation: Indira P. P. Bora, an exponent of Sattriya, Assam's classical dance, received the Padma Shri in 2020.

questions.text: Which article of the Constitution of India lays down that it shall be the duty of the Advocate-General to give advice to the Government of the State upon legal matters?
questions.explanation: Article 165 provides for an Advocate-General in each State, whose duty is to advise the State Government on legal matters.

questions.text: Which of the following peninsular rivers falls into the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: The Sabarmati flows into the Arabian Sea at the Gulf of Khambhat; the Mahanadi, Krishna and Godavari flow east into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.text: Follow On is related to which of the following cricket formats?
questions.explanation: The follow-on, which makes a side that trails well behind on first innings bat again at once, exists only in two-innings matches such as Tests.

questions.text: Who among the following rulers built five astronomical observatories at different places in north India?
questions.explanation: Sawai Jai Singh II of Amber (Jaipur) built the Jantar Mantar observatories at Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Mathura and Varanasi.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals is celebrated in Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Khajuraho Dance Festival is held at the Khajuraho temples in Madhya Pradesh. Thaipusam is celebrated in Tamil Nadu, Bihu in Assam and the Desert Festival at Jaisalmer in Rajasthan.

questions.text: In the ancient temple of Mahadev at Mahabaleshwar, the spout emerging from the mouth of a cow statue is the source of which river basin?
questions.explanation: The Krishna rises at Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats of Maharashtra, where the cow-mouth spout in the old Mahadev temple is taken as its source.

questions.text: Which is a serious contagious bacterial infection that usually affects the mucous membranes of the nose and throat?
questions.explanation: Diphtheria, caused by the bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae, attacks the mucous membranes of the nose and throat.

questions.text: Who among the following is a Sarod player popularly known as ‘Sarod Samrat’?
questions.explanation: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is known as 'Sarod Samrat'. Kishan Maharaj was a tabla player, Shivkumar Sharma a santoor player and Ravi Shankar a sitar player.

questions.text: What was a significant negative environmental impact of the Green Revolution?
questions.explanation: Heavy use of chemical fertilisers and pesticides, and over-irrigation, degraded the soil in Green Revolution areas through loss of fertility, salinity and waterlogging.

questions.text: What is subtracted from GDP to arrive at NDP?
questions.explanation: NDP = GDP − depreciation (the consumption of fixed capital).

questions.text: The Maharashtra Bhushan was conferred upon _________________ in the year 2002.
questions.explanation: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, the Hindustani vocalist, received the Maharashtra Bhushan, the state's highest civilian honour, in 2002.

questions.text: What is the tenure of office for the Chief Election Commissioner?
options: 5 years or up to the age of 60 years
6 years or up to the age of 60 years
6 years or up to the age of 65 years
5 years or up to the age of 65 years
questions.explanation: The Chief Election Commissioner holds office for six years or until the age of 65, whichever comes first.

questions.text: Which of the following animals was the emblem of the Chola dynasty?
questions.explanation: The tiger was the emblem of the Cholas; the fish was the Pandyas' and the bow the Cheras'.

questions.text: Which of the following does NOT belong to the category of Porifera?
questions.explanation: Hydra is a cnidarian (coelenterate). Spongilla, Euplectella and Sycon are sponges, phylum Porifera.

questions.text: Find the least value of x for which 57x716 is divisible by 9.
questions.explanation: The digit sum, 5 + 7 + x + 7 + 1 + 6 = 26 + x, must be a multiple of 9. The least is 27, so x = 1.

questions.text: AB and CD are two parallel chords drawn in a circle with centre O. The distance between the two chords is 21 cm. If the lengths of AB and CD are 24 cm and 18 cm, respectively, then the radius of the circle is equal to:
questions.explanation: The half-chords are 12 and 9 cm, at distances √(r² − 144) and √(r² − 81) from O. With the chords on opposite sides of O these add up to 21: r = 15 gives 9 + 12 = 21.

questions.text: For what value of k, the system of equations 4x + 12y + 36 = 0 and 5x + ky + 45 = 0 has an infinite number of solutions?
questions.explanation: For infinitely many solutions the coefficients must be in proportion: 4/5 = 12/k = 36/45. So k = 15.

questions.text: If the height and diameter of a cylinder are 12 cm and 28 cm, respectively, then find the ratio of the total surface area to the curved surface area.
In a company, the ratio of men and women is 5 : 3, respectively. When 150 additional women are employed in the company, the ratio becomes 5 : 4. How many men are employed in the company?
questions.explanation: With 5x men and 3x women, 5x : (3x + 150) = 5 : 4 gives 3x + 150 = 4x, so x = 150 and there are 750 men.

questions.text: In right-angled triangle ABC, ∠C=90, CM is perpendicular on AB. If AB = 18 cm and BM = 6 cm, then find the length of CM.
questions.explanation: AM = 18 − 6 = 12 cm. The altitude to the hypotenuse satisfies CM² = AM × BM = 12 × 6 = 72, so CM = 6√2 cm.

questions.text: A motorboat takes 18 hours to go downstream, and it takes 36 hours to return the same distance. Find the ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream.
questions.explanation: Over the same distance the speeds are in the ratio 2 : 1, so b + s = 2k and b − s = k. Then b = 1.5k and s = 0.5k: 3 : 1.

questions.text: In a rhombus PQRS, O is any interior point such that OP = OR. What is the degree measure of ∠SOQ?
questions.explanation: A point equidistant from P and R lies on the perpendicular bisector of PR, which in a rhombus is the diagonal QS. O is inside the rhombus, so it lies on QS between S and Q, and ∠SOQ is a straight angle: 180°.

questions.text: A group of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 62, and that of the rest is 76. What is the average score of the group?

Two candidates contested in an election. 80% of the voters cast their votes, out of which 5% of the polled votes were invalid. The winning candidate got 70% of valid votes and won by a majority of 36,480 votes. Find the total number of voters.
questions.explanation: Valid votes are 95% of 80% = 76% of the voters. The winner leads by 70% − 30% = 40% of these, which is 30.4% of the voters = 36,480, so there were 1,20,000 voters.

questions.text: A shopkeeper allows 40% discount on his goods. He further gives 20% discount. What is the single discount equivalent to these two successive discounts?
questions.explanation: After 40% and then 20% off, 0.6 × 0.8 = 0.48 of the price is left: a single discount of 52%.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom. To bring to light
questions.explanation: To 'bring to light' is to reveal or make known: to disclose.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. We should plan our actions “judiciously” before going to war.
questions.explanation: 'Judiciously' means with good judgement or sense; of the options, 'irrational', without reason or sense, is the opposite idea.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. The principal gave up / the prizes to / the winners on / Republic Day.
questions.explanation: Prizes are 'given away', that is handed out; 'give up' means to abandon or stop: 'The principal gave away the prizes'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words in the following sentence. Almost immediately, they heard the “high shrill piercing cry” of tires on the side road.
questions.explanation: A 'screech' is a loud, harsh, piercing cry or sound, such as tyres make when they skid.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Synthetic
questions.explanation: 'Synthetic' means man-made; its opposite is 'natural'. 'Artificial' and 'imitation' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the sentence given below. I “refuse” to let anything come in the way of my dreams.
questions.explanation: Here 'refuse' means to decline to allow; its opposite is 'permit'. 'Balk' is close to a synonym, and 'accord' (grant) is the opposite of 'refuse' only in the sense of refusing someone something.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. It was as simple as announcing what you have in your store or the services you offer in your premises. B. Over the years, advertising has evolved into a major industry that goes beyond informing to persuading and influencing. C. Advertising was initially meant to make people aware of the goods available in the market. D. It is a form of brainwashing consumers.
questions.explanation: C says what advertising was first meant for, A how simple that was, B how it has since grown into persuasion, and D sums it up: CABD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Attack
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'attack' is 'defence'. An 'ambush' is a surprise attack.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P) willing to go Q) is not R) my son S) camping
questions.explanation: 'My son (R) is not (Q) willing to go (P) camping (S).'

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (a) false news websites (b) spreading propaganda about politics (c) thrive because the advertisements and politicians (d) and social networking sites (e) make a lot of money
questions.explanation: 'False news websites (a) and social networking sites (d) thrive because the advertisements and politicians (c) spreading propaganda about politics (b) make a lot of money (e).'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. They have built a new bridge across the river.
options: A new bridge by them has been built across the river.
A new bridge has built across the river by them.
The river has been built a new bridge by them.
A new bridge has been built across the river by them.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'have built' becomes 'has been built', with the object, 'a new bridge', as the subject.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Experts acknowledged that some “counterfeiting of document” techniques are virtually impossible to detect.
questions.explanation: 'Forgery' is the counterfeiting of documents, signatures or money.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling to fill in the blank. The thought of eating half-cooked food under compulsion fills me with _____.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'repugnance', strong dislike or disgust.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in the brackets to fill in the blank. The chef requires ______ vegetables for the salad. [stale]
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'stale' is 'fresh', which also suits a salad.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. They are building a new hospital in the city.
options: A new hospital will be built in the city by them.
A new hospital was built in the city by them.
A new hospital is being built in the city by them.
A new hospital has been built in the city by them.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'are building' becomes 'is being built'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined part of the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. As the rulers of the planet, humans like to think that “it is the largest creatures” that will emerge victorious from the struggle for survival.
options: it is the most large creatures
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'they are the largest creatures', so that 'they' refers to the humans who see themselves as rulers of the planet. The original is itself a grammatical cleft sentence ('it is the largest creatures that will …'), so 'No substitution' is also arguable; 'the most large' and 'a largest creature' are wrong forms.

questions.text: Select the correct meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Rina “pulled a long face” since her husband had not bought her a diamond necklace on their anniversary.
questions.explanation: To 'pull a long face' is to look sad or disappointed.

questions.text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: Indian force are known for their loyalty and integrity.
It is said that Joseph was not ready to go to war.
It is impossible to wake Christine up in the morning.
Karl Marx was a renowned social scientist.
questions.explanation: 'Are' and 'their' need a plural subject: 'Indian forces are known for their loyalty and integrity.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. The ointment will help to _____ the wound.
questions.explanation: An ointment helps a wound to 'heal'; 'heel' (the back of the foot) and 'he'll' (he will) only sound the same.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence . The resturant offers a wide variety of dishes.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'restaurant'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The adverse (1)__________ of climate change and environmental degradation are increasingly driving human mobility the world over, particularly in countries with high exposure and low (2)__________ capacity. While most climate-related mobility currently occurs within countries, desperation and deteriorating environments can also compel people to seek a livelihood elsewhere through (3)__________ migration. While climate change negatively impacts everyone, everywhere, those already in vulnerable situations due to geography, poverty, gender, age, disability, origin, or other status, including migrant women who (4)__________ climate-sensitive livelihoods, and children who are less able to survive extreme weather events, are at the greatest risk of suffering harm. It is (5)__________ to recognise this reality and take meaningful action to protect the human rights of those most affected by climate change, including migrants.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The noun 'effects' (results) is needed: 'the adverse effects of climate change'. 'Affects' is a verb.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different. The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: KMOP, NPRS and EGIJ move +2, +2, +1 (K, M, O, P). UVXW moves +1, +2, −1, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Each of the letters in the word ‘MUSICAL’ is arranged in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical series between the letter which is third from the left end and the one which is third from the right end in the new letter-cluster thus formed?
questions.explanation: MUSICAL in alphabetical order is A C I L M S U. The third from the left is I and the third from the right is M; between them come J, K and L: three letters.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 17 : 67 21 : 79
questions.explanation: The second number is three times the first plus 16: 17 × 3 + 16 = 67 and 21 × 3 + 16 = 79. Likewise 34 × 3 + 16 = 118.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A x B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’. Based on the above, if ‘J + K ÷ L − T x R’, then how is J related to L?
questions.explanation: J is the mother of K, and K is the daughter of L. L is the brother of T, so male: L is K's father and J is L's wife.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (23, 230, 5) (17, 272, 8)
questions.explanation: The middle number is the product of the other two, doubled: 23 × 5 × 2 = 230 and 17 × 8 × 2 = 272. Likewise 19 × 8 × 2 = 304.

questions.text: Select the triad in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given triads. (54, 65, 76), (48, 59, 70) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is 11 more than the one before it: 54, 65, 76 and 48, 59, 70. Likewise 38, 49, 60.

questions.text: Three of the following four options are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does NOT belong to that group? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In the others the first and third numbers add up to three times the middle one: 118 + 161 = 3 × 93, 52 + 56 = 3 × 36 and 33 + 12 = 3 × 15. In 86 – 41 – 38, 86 + 38 = 124, not 123.

questions.text: Select the term from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. YL 93, XK 88, WJ 83, VI 78, ?
questions.explanation: Both letters move back one each time (Y, X, W, V, U and L, K, J, I, H) and the number falls by 5: UH 73.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some circles are rectangles. Some rectangles are squares. All squares are triangles. Conclusions: I. No circle is a triangle. II. Some rectangles are triangles. III. All rectangles are triangles.
options: Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: The rectangles that are squares are triangles, so some rectangles are triangles (II). Nothing fixes how the circles or the other rectangles stand to triangles, so I and III do not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'OASIS' is written as 'RJTBN' and 'OBESE' is written as 'DTFCN'. How will 'OCCUR’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed, then its first and last letters move back one and the middle three forward one: OASIS → SISAO → RJTBN. OCCUR → RUCCO → QVDDN.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘RUG’ is coded as ‘EPS’ and ‘SIT’ is coded as ‘RQG’. How will ‘COP’ be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves back 2 and the last one goes to the front: RUG → PSE → EPS and SIT → QGR → RQG. So COP → AMN → NAM.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 99 ÷ 41 + 208 × 2 – 35 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 99 × 41 − 208 ÷ 2 + 35 = 4059 − 104 + 35 = 3990.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. _ P _ J _ P _ P _ _ P _
questions.explanation: With J, P, P, J, P, J, P in the blanks the block JPP repeats: JPP JPP JPP JPP.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 1225, 1184, 1147, 1116, 1087, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −41, −37, −31, −29: the prime numbers in descending order. The next is −23: 1087 − 23 = 1064.

questions.text: ‘Meek’ is related to ‘Bold’ in the same way as ‘Spend’ is related to ‘________’. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.explanation: 'Meek' and 'Bold' are opposites; the opposite of 'Spend' is 'Hoard'.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? JKT, LJR, NIP, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +2 (J, L, N, P), second letters −1 (K, J, I, H) and third letters −2 (T, R, P, N): PHN.

questions.text: What will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 6 ÷ 8 – 91 × 13 + 30= ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 6 × 8 + 91 ÷ 13 − 30 = 48 + 7 − 30 = 25.

questions.text: Which fundamental duty applies on you when you see a few school students, on their educational trip to Humayun’s tomb, writing their names on the walls?
options: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
To defend the country and render national service
To protect and improve the natural environment
questions.explanation: Article 51A(i) makes it a fundamental duty to safeguard public property; Humayun's Tomb is a protected public monument.

questions.text: Identify the sequence of implementation of the following taxes. I.Land revenue II.Sales tax III.MODVAT IV.Service tax
questions.explanation: Land revenue is the oldest of these. Sales tax came in the provinces from 1939 (Madras was first), MODVAT in 1986 and service tax in 1994.

questions.text: Which Lavani singer got Padma Shri 2022 by the President of India?
questions.explanation: The veteran Lavani singer Sulochana Chavan received the Padma Shri in 2022.

questions.text: In the year 1925, who extracted lipids from an erythrocyte sample and found that lipid monolayers are good for measuring molecular surface area versus lateral pressure?
questions.explanation: In 1925 Gorter and Grendel spread the lipids extracted from red blood cells as a monolayer; it covered about twice the cells' surface area, which suggested that the membrane is a lipid bilayer.

questions.text: Which of the following is a species of tropical deciduous forests?
questions.explanation: Teak is a typical tree of the tropical deciduous forests; ebony and mahogany grow in the tropical evergreen forests.

questions.text: Who among the following was appointed as the Governor of Jharkhand in February 2023?
questions.explanation: C. P. Radhakrishnan was appointed Governor of Jharkhand in February 2023, succeeding Ramesh Bais, who moved to Maharashtra.

questions.text: Which of the following is the most acidic?
questions.explanation: Formic acid (HCOOH) is the strongest of these. In the others an alkyl group (CH₃, C₂H₅, C₃H₇) pushes electrons towards the carboxyl group, so it gives up its H⁺ less readily.

questions.text: What is the primary objective of the 'Standup India' initiative?
options: To support all types of startups
To facilitate bank loans for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs
questions.explanation: Stand-Up India (2016) facilitates bank loans of ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs setting up new enterprises.

questions.text: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India lays down that ‘The allocation of seats in the Council of States to be filled by representatives of the States and of the Union territories shall be in accordance with the provisions in that behalf contained in the fourth Schedule’?
questions.explanation: Article 80(2) allocates the seats of the states and union territories in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) according to the Fourth Schedule.

questions.text: Annapurna Devi is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Annapurna Devi, daughter of Ustad Allauddin Khan, was a celebrated player of the surbahar, the bass sitar.

questions.text: Where was the first women’s international test cricket match hosted in India in 1976?
questions.explanation: India's women played their first Test, against the West Indies, at Bangalore in 1976.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following founded the Atmiya Sabha in 1814?
questions.explanation: Raja Rammohun Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha in Calcutta; it was the forerunner of his Brahmo Sabha (1828).

questions.text: Matki dance is the famous folk dance associated with which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Matki is a folk dance of the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh, performed by women.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In the second Round Table Conference, Mahatma Gandhi represented which of the following parties?
questions.explanation: At the Second Round Table Conference (London, 1931) Gandhi was the sole representative of the Indian National Congress.

questions.text: Through which routes is the majority of India’s international trade carried out?
questions.explanation: Most of India's foreign trade, about 95% of it by volume, goes by sea; high-value and urgent goods go by air.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Nitric oxide (NO) is not a greenhouse gas; nitrous oxide (N₂O), methane and carbon dioxide are.

questions.text: What is the amount of financial assistance provided per month to girl students studying in government schools under the ‘Tamil Nadu Pudhumai Penn Scheme’ launched by the Government of Tamil Nadu in 2023?
questions.explanation: Under Pudhumai Penn, girls who studied in government schools from Class 6 to 12 get ₹1,000 a month while they pursue higher education.

questions.text: Which of the following options indicates the size of PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms)?
questions.explanation: PPLO (mycoplasma) are among the smallest living cells; NCERT gives their size as about 0.1 µm.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, ‘Other Religions and Persuasions (ORP)’ comprise how much of the population?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 counted about 7.9 million people (0.66%) under Other Religions and Persuasions.

questions.text: Under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, the maximum premium payable by the farmers will be _________ for all kharif food and oilseeds crops.
questions.explanation: Under PMFBY farmers pay at most 2% of the sum insured for kharif crops, 1.5% for rabi crops and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops.

questions.text: The Maukharis ruled over which of the following cities in western Uttar Pradesh that over the time replaced Pataliputra as a political centre of north India?
questions.explanation: The Maukharis ruled from Kannauj, which later became Harsha's capital and took Pataliputra's place as the political centre of north India.

questions.text: Which allotrope of carbon was discovered by Robert F Curl, Harold W Kroto and Richard E Smalley in 1985?
questions.explanation: Curl, Kroto and Smalley discovered buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀) in 1985 and shared the 1996 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for it.

questions.text: Under which of the following Pala king's patronage the Vikramshila university in 8th century India was founded?
questions.explanation: The Pala king Dharmapala founded the Vikramshila university in Bihar.

questions.text: Kajari Mahotsav is primarily celebrated in which of the following districts of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Mirzapur, the district best known for Kajari, the folk songs of the rainy season.

questions.text: When was the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award renamed as Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award?
questions.explanation: The Khel Ratna was renamed after Major Dhyan Chand on 6 August 2021.

questions.text: In a bank, 6% interest is given on the deposited amount. The bank then invests the money in the stock market and is able to earn ₹30,000 for every ₹3,00,000. How much money is the bank earning finally if the total amount deposited in the bank is ₹60,00,000?
In a triangle, the lengths of sides are 6 units, 12 units and x units. How many possible integer values are there for x?
questions.explanation: The third side lies between 12 − 6 = 6 and 12 + 6 = 18, so x = 7, 8, …, 17: 11 values.

questions.text: Arvind and Chetan started running simultaneously from the same point in the same direction on a circular track of length 210 m. If Arvind takes 180 seconds to complete one round, and Chetan takes 420 seconds to complete one round, after how much time will they meet for the first time at the starting point on the track?
questions.explanation: They are together at the start again after LCM(180, 420) = 1260 seconds = 21 minutes.

questions.text: Find the length of the longest diagonal (in cm) of a cuboidal box of dimensions 1.2 cm × 1.3 cm × 1.5 cm (correct to two decimal places).
A circular arc makes an angle of 15° at the centre. If the radius of the circular arc is 14 cm, what is the perimeter (correct up to two decimal places) of the sector so formed? (π = 3.14)?

Two pipes can fill a tank in 12 hours and 18 hours, respectively, while a third pipe can empty it in 8 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill the empty tank if all three pipes are opened simultaneously?
questions.explanation: In an hour the tank gains 1/12 + 1/18 − 1/8 = (6 + 4 − 9)/72 = 1/72 of itself, so it fills in 72 hours.

questions.text: If P is a digit such that 6954P is divisible by 11, then P equals:
questions.explanation: For 11 the difference between the sums of alternate digits must be a multiple of 11: (6 + 5 + P) − (9 + 4) = P − 2, so P = 2.

questions.text: 42 litres of milk at ₹25 per litre is mixed with 28 litres of milk at ₹40 per litre. Find the average price of the mixture.
In triangle ABC, D is the mid-point of BC. If DL perpendicular to AB and DM perpendicular to AC such that DL = DM, then the triangle will be:
questions.explanation: Triangles DLB and DMC are right-angled with DB = DC and DL = DM, so they are congruent (RHS) and ∠B = ∠C. Then AB = AC.

questions.text: There are y yellow marbles and b blue marbles in a box. 18% of the yellow marbles were added to 24% of the blue marbles, and the total was 30. Three times the number of yellow marbles exceeds two times the number of blue marbles by 200. What is the ratio of y² to b²?
questions.explanation: 0.18y + 0.24b = 30 gives 3y + 4b = 500; subtracting 3y − 2b = 200 leaves 6b = 300, so b = 50 and y = 100. y² : b² = 10000 : 2500 = 4 : 1.

questions.text: A function of two variable varies directly with x and inversely with y. Determine function when x = 5 and y = 3. Given that, for x = 0 and y = 1, f = 15 and for x = 1 and y = 15, f = 2.
questions.explanation: A single product kx/y would be 0 at x = 0, so f is a direct part plus an inverse part: f = ax + b/y. x = 0, y = 1 gives b = 15, and x = 1, y = 15 gives a + 1 = 2, so a = 1. Then f = 5 + 15/3 = 10.

questions.text: The marked price of a TV set is ₹18,500. If the dealer allows two successive discounts of 20% and 5%, for how much is the TV available?
If a triangle has a perimeter of 52 units, then all its sides have length ________ units.
questions.explanation: Each side is less than the sum of the other two, so twice any side is less than the perimeter: every side is under 26. A side of 25 is possible (25, 14, 13), so no smaller bound holds.

questions.text: In how many years will ₹7,200 amount to ₹8,928 at a simple interest rate of 8% per annum?
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cut corners
options: Do something in an inexpensive and easy way
questions.explanation: To 'cut corners' is to do something in the cheapest or easiest way, often at the cost of quality.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. By whom were you injured?
questions.explanation: The simple past passive 'were you injured' becomes the simple past active, with 'by whom' becoming 'who': 'Who injured you?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. The movie's plot was “predictable”, with clichéd twists and turns.
questions.explanation: 'Predictable' means expected; its opposite is 'unexpected'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. I was completely “mesmerised” by the performance.
questions.explanation: 'Mesmerised' means held spellbound: 'fascinated'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Easy does it
options: Used to tell someone to do something horridly
Used to tell someone to do something violently
Used to tell someone to do something rarely
Used to tell someone to do something slowly and carefully
questions.explanation: 'Easy does it' tells someone to go slowly and carefully.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Candid
questions.explanation: 'Candid' means frank and honest; its opposite is 'dishonest'. 'Guileless' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who deceives others by pretending to be someone else
questions.explanation: An impostor deceives others by pretending to be someone else; 'fraud' is broader, any deceiver or deception.

questions.text: Select the sentence that does NOT have a spelling error.
options: The author is famous for leading a life of subterfuge and contredictions which has led to challenges in understanding past works.
Statistical patterns and historical data cannot predict the futristic problems that await a civilisation like ours.
The new caches of materials reveal a secret pleascence that was hidden away from the rest of the world
Many friends and memoirists have described the author in detail but there are no photos of the author available to the press.
questions.explanation: The other sentences misspell 'contradictions', 'futuristic' and 'pleasance' (a secluded garden).

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A thing fit to eat.
questions.explanation: 'Edible' means fit to be eaten.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Having known that / the train was already on the platform, / they ran fastly / to catch it.
options: the train was already on the platform
questions.explanation: 'Fast' is both adjective and adverb, and 'fastly' is not a word: 'they ran fast'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The patient was suffering from a “chronic” disease.
questions.explanation: 'Chronic' describes an illness that lasts a long time and is often serious. Its strict opposite, 'acute' (short-lived), is not offered; SSC's key gives 'mild', the one option opposed to a serious, lasting illness.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. If it had not rained, they “would not postpone” the programmes.
questions.explanation: An unreal past condition takes 'would have' with the past participle: 'If it had not rained, they would not have postponed the programmes.'

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Capable of being done
questions.explanation: 'Feasible' means possible to do or carry out.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Reluctant
questions.explanation: 'Reluctant' means unwilling; its opposite is 'enthusiastic'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. The workers received “a sum for the services they rendered.”
questions.explanation: Remuneration is payment for work or services.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Were the plants being grafted by the gardener?
options: Was the gardener grafting the plants?
Were the gardener grafting the plants?
Was the gardener grafted the plants?
Were the plants grafting the gardener?
questions.explanation: The past continuous passive 'were … being grafted' becomes the past continuous active, with the singular subject taking 'was': 'Was the gardener grafting the plants?'

questions.text: Identify the error in the following sentence. Brr, the city view from the Eiffel Tower is amazing!
questions.explanation: 'Brr' expresses feeling cold, which does not fit admiration of the view; an interjection such as 'Wow' does.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Foul smell will come if the food is “not fresh”.
questions.explanation: Food that is not fresh is 'stale'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. Educational technology has become a necesity if one desires excellent output.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'necessity'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Rory Cooper was a top aide to former House Majority Leader Eric Cantor, the up-and-coming Virginia Republican who lost a 2014 House primary. He was also a prominent Never Trumper, openly (1)______________ how awful he found the 45th president. The cause Cooper has (2)______________ himself to for the past year, though, is closer to home. He is, as he puts it in his Twitter bio, ‘Apparently Mr. Open the Schools’. A father of a fifth grader, a second grader and a kindergartner, Cooper is (3) ___________ because the public schools in Fairfax, Virginia, where he lives, have not reopened. Fairfax, in the Washington, D.C., suburbs, is one of the school districts that has moved (4) ___________ toward in-person learning, and it is still not close: only in the past few weeks have students started to return to classrooms, and only about half of those eligible have opted to go back, for an (5) ________________ of two days a week.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1
questions.explanation: He was openly 'detailing', setting out at length, how awful he found the president.

Rory Cooper was a top aide to former House Majority Leader Eric Cantor, the up-and-coming Virginia Republican who lost a 2014 House primary. He was also a prominent Never Trumper, openly (1)______________ how awful he found the 45th president. The cause Cooper has (2)______________ himself to for the past year, though, is closer to home. He is, as he puts it in his Twitter bio, ‘Apparently Mr. Open the Schools’. Fairfax, in the Washington, D.C., suburbs, is one of the school districts that has moved (4) ___________ toward in-person learning, and it is still not close: only in the past few weeks have students started to return to classrooms, and only about half of those eligible have opted to go back, for an (5) ________________ of two days a week.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3

questions.text: Select the option that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. AH21, CJ18, EL15, GN12, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move 2 places forward (A, C, E, G, I), second letters too (H, J, L, N, P), and the numbers fall by 3 (21, 18, 15, 12, 9): IP9.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Frivolous : Big :: Deride : ?
questions.explanation: 'Frivolous' (trivial, of little importance) is the opposite of 'big' (important). Likewise the opposite of 'deride' (mock) is 'encourage'; 'taunt' and 'jeer' mean the same as 'deride'.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 30, 20, ?, 60, 140

Select the pair in which the numbers are related to each other in the same way as are the numbers in the given pairs. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 3 : 25 4 : 62
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first minus 2: 3³ − 2 = 25 and 4³ − 2 = 62. Likewise 5³ − 2 = 123.

questions.text: The position(s) of how many letters will remain unchanged if all the letters in the word ‘GRIMACE’ are arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: GRIMACE in alphabetical order is A C E G I M R. Position by position (G/A, R/C, I/E, M/G, A/I, C/M, E/R) no letter stays where it was.

questions.text: ‘Ample’ is related to ‘Abundant’ in the same way as ‘Substantial’ is related to ‘________’. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.explanation: 'Ample' and 'abundant' mean the same; so do 'substantial' and 'considerable'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘HUSBAND’ is written as ‘JVUDBPF’ and ‘SISTER’ is written as ‘UJUVFT’. How will ‘BROTHER’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Consonants move 2 places forward and vowels 1: HUSBAND → JVUDBPF and SISTER → UJUVFT. So BROTHER → DTPVJFT.

questions.text: In a certain code language, X + Y means ‘X is the father of Y’, X − Y means ‘X is the brother of Y’, X × Y means ‘X is the sister of Y’, X ÷ Y means ‘X is the wife of Y’. Based on the above, how is D related to H if ‘D × E ÷ F + G − H’?
questions.explanation: F is the father of G and G the brother of H, so F is H's father and E, F's wife, is H's mother. D is E's sister, so D is H's mother's sister.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. _ X _ F _ _ _ X T _ X _
questions.explanation: With F, T, X, T, F, F, T in the blanks the block FXT repeats: FXT FXT FXT FXT.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘mountain stand tall’ is coded as ‘33 66 44’; ‘rocky is tall’ is coded as ‘44 55 11’ and ‘rocky is mountain’ is coded as ‘33 55 11’. How is ‘stand’ coded in that language?
questions.explanation: 'tall' is in the first two sentences and 44 in both codes, so tall = 44; 'mountain' is in the first and third and 33 in both, so mountain = 33. That leaves stand = 66.

questions.text: Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 31 – 5 – 160, 13 – 8 – 109 and 21 – 4 – 89 the third number is the product of the first two plus 5 (155 + 5, 104 + 5, 84 + 5). 27 × 9 = 243 with nothing added, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. D _ F D _ F _ F _ D _ F
questions.explanation: With F, F, D, F, F in the blanks the block DFF repeats: DFF DFF DFF DFF.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: In NMI, YXT and SRN the letters move 1 back, then 4 back. LKF moves 1 back, then 5 back, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 315 × 15 − 93 + 16 ÷ 7 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 315 ÷ 15 + 93 − 16 × 7 = 21 + 93 − 112 = 2.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (27, 405, 3) (23, 690, 6)
questions.explanation: The middle number is the product of the other two times 5: 27 × 3 × 5 = 405 and 23 × 6 × 5 = 690. Likewise 24 × 5 × 5 = 600.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. 7 — 14 — 23 4 — 11 — 20 NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each set adds 7, then 9: 7, 14, 23 and 4, 11, 20. Likewise 5, 12, 21.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? KES, MIQ, PMN, TQJ, YUE, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +2, +3, +4, +5, so next +6: Y → E. Second letters move +4: U → Y. Third letters move −2, −3, −4, −5, so next −6: E → Y. EYY.

questions.text: Which team won the T20 cricket event, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy 2022-2023?
questions.explanation: Mumbai won the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy 2022-23, beating Himachal Pradesh in the final.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, which group of Union Territories recorded the highest sex ratio?
options: Puducherry, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Puducherry, Delhi, Andaman and Nicobar Islands
questions.explanation: In the 2011 census Puducherry, Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands had the highest sex ratios of the Union Territories, Puducherry (1,037 females per 1,000 males) the only one above 1,000; Delhi and Chandigarh were lower.

questions.text: Which Indian singer wrote ‘Raag Sarita’?
questions.explanation: 'Raag Sarita', a collection of his own bandishes with notation, is by the Hindustani vocalist Pandit C. R. (Chintaman Raghunath) Vyas.

questions.text: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution was borrowed from Irish Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

questions.text: Which state government honoured Vani Jairam with the MS Subbulakshmi Award for 2019?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Tamil Nadu, whose government presents an award named after M. S. Subbulakshmi to musicians alongside its Kalaimamani awards.

questions.text: Vindhyashakti was the founder of which of the following dynasties?
questions.explanation: Vindhyashakti founded the Vakataka dynasty in the Deccan in the 3rd century AD.

questions.text: Which of the following is a man-made ecosystem?
questions.explanation: An aquarium is made and maintained by people; forests, grasslands and deserts are natural ecosystems.

questions.text: Which of the following are the two basic categories of an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Ecosystems fall into two basic categories, terrestrial (forest, grassland, desert) and aquatic (pond, lake, wetland, river, estuary).

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct about the composition of the agriculture sector and employment in GDP post-independence?
options: The proportion of both the agriculture sector and employment in GDP has declined significantly.
The proportion of employment has declined significantly but not the share of the agriculture sector in GDP.
The proportion of both the agriculture sector and employment in GDP has increased significantly.
The proportion of GDP contributed by the agricultural sector declined significantly but not the employment depending on the agriculture sector.
questions.explanation: NCERT notes that agriculture's share of GDP fell sharply in the decades after independence, while the share of the population depending on it barely fell.

questions.text: Who among the following famous Indian women cricketers announced retirement in June 2022?
questions.explanation: Mithali Raj announced her retirement from international cricket in June 2022; Jhulan Goswami retired later that year.

questions.text: Which region in India receives less rainfall in summer, but heavy rainfall in winter season due to the retreating north easterly winds?
questions.explanation: The Coromandel coast (Tamil Nadu), on the east, gets little rain from the summer monsoon and much of its rain in October-December from the retreating north-east winds.

questions.text: Sundari trees are found in which type of forests in India?
questions.explanation: Sundari trees grow in the mangrove forests of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta, the Sundarbans, which are named after them.

questions.text: The Supreme Court of India comprises the Chief Justice and not more than ______ other Judges appointed by the President of India.
questions.explanation: Since the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019 the Court has the Chief Justice and up to 33 other judges, 34 in all.

questions.text: Who won the paralympic bronze medal in archery for India at Tokyo in 2020?
questions.explanation: Harvinder Singh won bronze in men's individual recurve archery at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, India's first Paralympic archery medal.

questions.text: The central bank of India or Reserve Bank of India was created before Independence, in the year 1934. The recommendation to create a central bank was made by a commission called:
questions.explanation: The Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, 1926) recommended a central bank; the RBI Act followed in 1934 and the Bank opened in 1935.

questions.text: Ranjana Gauhar was awarded the Padma Shri Award (2003) for her contribution to which of the following Indian dance forms?
questions.explanation: Ranjana Gauhar is an Odissi dancer; she received the Padma Shri in 2003.

questions.text: Which of the following two quantities have the same dimensions?
options: Power and radius of circular motion
questions.explanation: Work (force × distance) and torque (force × perpendicular distance) both have the dimensions [ML²T⁻²].

questions.text: Which polyatomic ionic compound is a white, crystalline powder used in fire extinguishers and to neutralise acids and bases?
questions.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate (baking soda, NaHCO₃) is a white crystalline powder; it gives off carbon dioxide in soda-acid fire extinguishers, and its hydrogencarbonate ion reacts with both acids and bases.

questions.text: Which port is developed as a satellite port?
questions.explanation: The Jawaharlal Nehru Port at Nhava Sheva was developed as a satellite port to relieve the pressure on Mumbai port.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Doctrine of Lapse was an annexation policy devised by which of the following Governor-Generals of India?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie used the Doctrine of Lapse to annex states whose rulers died without a natural heir, such as Satara and Jhansi.

questions.text: Chhath Puja is the main festival of which state?
questions.explanation: Chhath Puja, in honour of the Sun god, is the main festival of Bihar.

questions.text: For which of the following states was the Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022, introduced in the Parliament?
questions.explanation: The bill moved the Gond community in four districts of Uttar Pradesh (Chandauli, Kushinagar, Sant Kabir Nagar and Sant Ravidas Nagar) from the state's Scheduled Castes list to its Scheduled Tribes list.

questions.text: Who among the following is the hero of the Sanskrit historical poem, the 'Ramacharita' written by Sandhyakar Nandi?
questions.explanation: Sandhyakar Nandi's 'Ramacharita' tells the story of the Ramayana and, in parallel, of the Pala king Ramapala.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following areas did the Uprising of Khurda in 1817 take place?
questions.explanation: The Paika Rebellion of 1817, led by Bakshi Jagabandhu, broke out at Khurda in Odisha against the East India Company.

questions.text: A shopkeeper mixes two types of rice costing ₹250/5 kg and ₹280/5 kg in the ratio 7 : 8. Find the net cost of the resultant mixture (per kg).
questions.explanation: The two kinds cost ₹50 and ₹56 a kg. (7 × 50 + 8 × 56)/15 = 798/15 = ₹53.20 a kg.

questions.text: There are two pipes used to fill a tank and when operated together, they can fill the tank in 20 minutes. If one pipe can fill the tank two and a half times as quickly as the other, then the faster pipe alone can fill the tank in:
questions.explanation: If the slower pipe fills x of the tank a minute, the faster fills 2.5x: 3.5x = 1/20, so x = 1/70 and the faster pipe fills 2.5/70 = 1/28 a minute: 28 minutes.

questions.text: At a cafe, Rama bought drinks for her 7 friends at ₹240. Some of them wanted coffee, while others wanted black tea. A regular cup of coffee cost ₹40 and a regular cup of black tea cost ₹30. How many cups of tea did she purchase?
questions.explanation: If she bought t cups of tea, 30t + 40(7 − t) = 240, so 280 − 10t = 240 and t = 4.

questions.text: In an election between R and S, R gets 110% of the votes of S and beats S by 770 votes. If there were no invalid votes, then the total number of votes polled is:
questions.explanation: R − S = 10% of S = 770, so S = 7,700 and R = 8,470: 16,170 votes in all.

questions.text: A and B are centres of two circles with radii 2 cm and 1 cm respectively, where AB = 5 cm. C is the centre of another circle of radius r cm, which touches each of the above two circles externally. If ∠ACB=90° , then the value of r is:
questions.explanation: Circles touching externally have their centres the sum of the radii apart: AC = 2 + r and BC = 1 + r. With ∠ACB = 90°, (2 + r)² + (1 + r)² = 5², so r² + 3r − 10 = 0 and r = 2.

questions.text: If the successive discount by 10%,15%, then the single equivalent rate of discount is:
Simplify the following expression. [{70 − 60÷ 2 of 6} + (20− 10)÷ 10] + 600÷ 25 of (2 ×3)× (2 of 3) + 2 of 5.
questions.explanation: 'Of' comes first: 60 ÷ 12 = 5, so the square bracket is (70 − 5) + 10 ÷ 10 = 66. Then 600 ÷ 150 × 6 = 24 and 2 of 5 = 10: 66 + 24 + 10 = 100.

questions.text: If 321y72 is a multiple of 6, where y is a digit, what is the least value of y?
questions.explanation: A number divisible by 6 is even and divisible by 3. 321y72 is even, and its digit sum 15 + y is divisible by 3 for y = 0, 3, 6 or 9: the least is 0.

questions.text: If A:B = 6 : 8 and B:C = 5 : 10, then A:B:C is:
The solution of the following equations is: 5x + 4y - 8z = 1 7x - 9y + z = - 1 2x + 3y - 4z = 1
questions.explanation: x = y = z = 1 satisfies all three: 5 + 4 − 8 = 1, 7 − 9 + 1 = −1 and 2 + 3 − 4 = 1.

questions.text: A boat can travel 78 km upstream and back in a total of 32 hours. It can travel 15 km upstream and 52 km downstream in a total of 9 hours. How much distance will the boat cover in 12 hours in still water?
questions.explanation: With a = 1/upstream speed and b = 1/downstream speed, 78(a + b) = 32 and 15a + 52b = 9 give a = 1/3 and b = 1/13. The speeds are 3 and 13 km/h, so the boat's own speed is (3 + 13)/2 = 8 km/h: 8 × 12 = 96 km.

questions.text: Pranav borrows a sum of ₹6,23,305 at the rate of 10% per annum simple interest. At the end of the first year, he repays ₹16,390 towards return of principal amount borrowed. If Pranav clears all pending dues at the end of the second year, including interest payment that accrued during the first year, how much does he pay (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
questions.explanation: Year 1 interest is 10% of ₹6,23,305 = ₹62,330.50. After the ₹16,390 repayment the principal is ₹6,06,915, which earns ₹60,691.50 in year 2. Due at the end: 6,06,915 + 62,330.50 + 60,691.50 = ₹7,29,937.

questions.text: In the following sentence, four words have been underlined, out of which one word is MISSPELT. Select the option with the MISSPELT word. In spite of the “dilemma” that “preveiled” during the discussion sessions, the “committee” remained committed to finding an “amicable” solution to the issue.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'prevailed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A bad patch
options: A dangerous road to walk on
A person who takes a difficult path
A period of time when a person faces lots of troubles
questions.explanation: 'A bad patch' is a period of difficulty or trouble.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A written statement made under oath
questions.explanation: An affidavit is a written statement confirmed by oath, for use as evidence in court.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Barbarity
questions.explanation: 'Barbarity' is extreme cruelty; its opposite is 'compassion'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Attributes', with a double 't'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The team always anticipate a bowling friendly “pitch on their easy victory” in the T20 matches.
questions.explanation: Something wanted as the means to an end is wanted 'for' it: a bowling-friendly pitch 'for' their easy victory.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The team will announce the winner tomorrow.
options: The winner will be announced by the team tomorrow.
The winner will announce tomorrow by the team.
Tomorrow will be announced the winner by the team.
The team will announce tomorrow the winner.
questions.explanation: 'Will announce' becomes 'will be announced', with the object 'the winner' as the subject and the agent after 'by'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Mr. Surya / have no interior / motive in offering / you support.
questions.explanation: A singular subject takes 'has', and a hidden reason is an 'ulterior' motive: 'Mr. Surya has no ulterior motive in offering you support.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. By the end of / this month, he / will been working / for five years.
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous is 'will have been working': 'By the end of this month, he will have been working for five years.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Kamal is not willing to purchase a house on the 12th floor of a sea-side apartment, as she is fearful of heights. She is suffering from ___________.
questions.explanation: Acrophobia is the fear of heights; claustrophobia is the fear of closed spaces and heliophobia the fear of sunlight.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. An elephant is a “large” mammal.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'large' is 'tiny'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Epitome
questions.explanation: Besides a perfect example, an 'epitome' is a summary or abridgement of a written work; its opposite is an 'expansion'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Cannot be corrected
questions.explanation: 'Incorrigible' means not able to be corrected or reformed; 'illegible' means unreadable and 'ineligible' not qualified.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A. Smoking in B. Your youth stunts C. The body and D. Clouds the brain
questions.explanation: 'Smoking in (A) your youth stunts (B) the body and (C) clouds the brain (D).'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Don’t let Dylan fool you!
options: Do not ever be fooled by Dylan.
Do not be fool by Dylan.
Do not be fooled by Dylan.
Do not have been fooled by Dylan.
questions.explanation: 'Don't let Dylan fool you' becomes 'Do not be fooled by Dylan'; adding 'ever' changes the meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. Satya is always “great” to his friends who helped him when he was in trouble.
questions.explanation: Thankful to someone for help is 'grateful'; 'greatful' is a misspelling.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in bold to fill in the blank. The modern work is deliberately ________ (ambiguous).
questions.explanation: 'Ambiguous' means open to more than one meaning; its opposite is 'certain'. 'Dubious', 'vague' and 'puzzling' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The homophone for the word ‘there’ is _________.
questions.explanation: 'Their' sounds the same as 'there' but differs in meaning and spelling: a homophone.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Turned a deaf ear to
questions.explanation: To 'turn a deaf ear to' something is to refuse to listen to it: to disregard it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Sleeping, dreaming and waking are three important (1)_______ for ordinary humans. But for those who have (2)_______ transcendental knowledge, all three are almost same and there is not much difference among these three. ‘The world and life is a myth and it keeps on changing’ (3)_______ Adi Shankaracharya, the greatest ‘Advaita’ preacher. Ramana Maharshi observed no difference between dreaming and waking states. What he said is that it is from one unreal world to another (4)_______ world. There is no difference between the images one sees when waking up and the images he/she sees during dreams. According to this great sage of the modern century, the first one is daydream and the second one is a night dream. The usual philosophers say that mind and body are the two elements and mind is the source of all diverse thoughts. In the waking up state, the mind is active with all tensions and dissatisfactions, so happiness is missing: during sleep as the mind is absent and so is the physical world, the real happiness (5)______. It is said that deep sleep, where there is no feeling of body, mind and the world, is the natural state of human beings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Sleeping, dreaming and waking are three important 'aspects' (sides or states) of ordinary human life.

It is said that deep sleep, where there is no feeling of body, mind and the world, is the natural state of human beings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The quotation is followed by its speaker in the present tense: '… says Adi Shankaracharya'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Sleeping, dreaming and waking are three important (1)_______ for ordinary humans. But for those who have (2)_______ transcendental knowledge, all three are almost same and there is not much difference among these three. ‘The world and life is a myth and it keeps on changing’ (3)_______ Adi Shankaracharya, the greatest ‘Advaita’ preacher. Ramana Maharshi observed no difference between dreaming and waking states. What he said is that it is from one unreal world to another (4)_______ world. There is no difference between the images one sees when waking up and the images he/she sees during dreams. According to this great sage of the modern century, the first one is daydream and the second one is a night dream. The usual philosophers say that mind and body are the two elements and mind is the source of all diverse thoughts. In the waking up state, the mind is active with all tensions and dissatisfactions, so happiness is missing: during sleep as the mind is absent and so is the physical world, the real happiness (5)______. It is said that deep sleep, where there is no feeling of body, mind and the world, is the natural state of human beings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: From one unreal world to another 'unreal' world, repeating the adjective.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Sleeping, dreaming and waking are three important (1)_______ for ordinary humans. But for those who have (2)_______ transcendental knowledge, all three are almost same and there is not much difference among these three. ‘The world and life is a myth and it keeps on changing’ (3)_______ Adi Shankaracharya, the greatest ‘Advaita’ preacher. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The present passive fits the general statement: during sleep 'the real happiness is gained'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GLOBAL' is written as '221714272817', 'FOREST' is written as '23141124109', how will 'IMPACT' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is coded by its position counted from Z (Z = 1, A = 26) plus 2: G = 20 + 2 = 22, L = 15 + 2 = 17 and so on. IMPACT: I = 18 + 2 = 20, M = 16, P = 13, A = 28, C = 26, T = 9, giving 20161328269.

questions.text: Select the triad in which the numbers are related to each other in the same way as the numbers in the following triads. 16-40-100 8-20-50 (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is 2.5 times the one before: 16 → 40 → 100 and 8 → 20 → 50. Likewise 24 → 60 → 150.
